rows.name: LocalLaw.reads (structure field)
rows.states: For every exchange e, any two configurations s and s' that agree on every relatum e touches, and any relatum x that e touches: the state e's action gives x from s equals the state it gives x from s'. So what an exchange makes of a touched relatum depends only on the states of the relata it touches (with keeps, untouched relata are left as they were).
rows.shape: STRUCTURE FIELD of LocalLaw X E σ, type ∀ e s s' x, (∀ y, touches e y = true → s y = s' y) → touches e x = true → act e s x = act e s' x (a proof obligation, a Prop-valued field).
rows.beside: none found by name in this module or its imports (World, Reordering): the field is a footprint-locality condition, the same kind of relation as Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn (a step's outcome determined by a projection of the state), but Mechanism is not imported and no theorem ties them. Within the module the field is used in the commuting of exchanges with disjoint footprints (lines 255, 275, 284, 1000, 1008); reads_renumber and world_renumber_reads carry a hypothesis of the same shape (∀ l l', agree on touched relata → R l → R l') under the local name 'reads'.
rows.docstring: "it touches determine (`reads`)." (from: "Exchanges acting locally on relata: each exchange touches some relata, leaves every other relatum's state as it was (`keeps`), and changes a relatum it touches as the states of the relata it touches determine (`reads`).")

rows.name: Relay.reads
rows.states: A fixed relation from the three nodes (source, relay, reader) to the two conditions (first, second): it holds exactly for (relay, first) and (reader, second), false otherwise. It is supplied as the level-coupling relation `obs` of TimedResponse, so it says which condition's level couples into which node.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on Node × Spot (a function Node → Spot → Prop).
rows.beside: It is the `obs` argument of TimedResponse.CoupledIntoAt (W.requires s g c ∨ obs g c) and of Testing.CoupledInto (W.DependsOn g c ∨ obs g c); so 'n reads c' is 'c is coupled by level into n'. Tied in Relay.reader_far (CoupledIntoAt (web false) reads .reader s c → ... 2 < 1 + n), not_reached_at_two and reached_at_three.
rows.docstring: "The relay is coupled by level into the first condition, the reader into the second."

rows.name: Relay.readAt
rows.states: Given a step t and a level history l, the Boolean whether the level of the second condition at step t is positive. Its value depends only on l at (t, second).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Nat × (Nat → Spot → Nat) to Bool.
rows.beside: It is an instance of the `read` parameter of TimedResponse.answer_alike_far, whose premise is that the answer is equal on histories AlikeThroughUpTo obs g (Testing.AlikeThroughUpTo: alike at every step up to t on the conditions coupled into g). No theorem in the module proves readAt respects AlikeThroughUpTo; the theorem about it is Relay.answers_two_and_three (equal at step 2 between web false and web true, different at step 3).
rows.docstring: "The reader reads the second condition."

rows.name: Reader (structure)
rows.states: One role's part of the joint law: a weight for each candidate world, a value of going on and a value of switching off at each world under each valuation state, a map from a world to what a demonstration there shows, and a revision of the valuation state by a presented input. With it, Reader.update filters the listing by what a demonstration shows or revises the valuation by a presented input, and Reader.answerOf gives the Bool answer of a (listing, valuation) state.
rows.shape: STRUCTURE Reader W V O X with fields weight : W → Nat, goVal : V → W → Nat, offVal : V → W → Nat, reveal : W → O, revalue : V → X → V.
rows.beside: No relational name; it is the counterpart of Holder (the other role's part) and the two are combined by joint on Blanket.Blanketed, where this role's state is the internal part and it depends on the holding role only through Input (Reader.input), and the holding role depends on it only through the answer. No theorem renames it; the module's prose names it 'the reading formation'.
rows.docstring: "**The reading role's part of the joint law**: the weights on candidate worlds, the values of going"

rows.name: reading (WeightsApart.reading and OneListing.reading)
rows.states: Two worked-example definitions, each a Model: WeightsApart.reading lists candidates 0, 1, 2 with weights 1, 2, 2 (against holding's 2, 1, 1); OneListing.reading lists false and true each weighted 1 (against holding's single candidate false). Each is the second role's model of candidates, set beside the holding role's model.
rows.shape: A LIST of members with weights (Model Nat, Model Bool: a list of candidates and a weight function).
rows.beside: none found; it is a constant named by role, compared with the sibling constant `holding` in the same namespace (WeightsApart, OneListing); no relation name stands for it.
rows.docstring: "The reading formation's model: the same candidates weighted 1, 2 and 2." (WeightsApart); "The reading formation lists both, each weighted one." (OneListing)

rows.name: Frame.ReadsAt
rows.states: Along run r, for claim c, time τ and a relation support between states and claims: at every step t from τ on, c is realized in r's state at t if and only if support holds of c in r's state at τ. So realization of c from τ onward is fixed by one fact at τ.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (Frame, Run, claim c, time τ, support : S → C → Prop).
rows.beside: readsAt_iff_settled: (∃ support, F.ReadsAt r c τ support) ↔ ∀ t ≥ τ, (realized at t ↔ realized at τ), i.e. realization of c is constant from τ on (stated inline, no separate name; Frontier.Settled and Remainder.SettledFrom are different relations). Also ReadsAt.loss_retained (missed at τ → not realized at any later t) and not_readsAt_of_recovery.
rows.docstring: "Along the run `r`, claim `c` is read at time `τ`: from `τ` on, `c` is realized exactly where `support` held of it at `τ`."

rows.name: Agree.readBoth
rows.states: A likelihood: for each coin bias (heads, fair, tails) and each pair of toss outcomes, a weight in sixteenths (heads-biased: 9,3,3,1; fair: 4 each; tails-biased: 1,3,3,9). Its weights differ between the heads- and tails-biased coins, unlike `agreeing`, which gives both biases the same weights.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Bias × (Bool × Bool) to Nat.
rows.beside: Tied (same module): Tied lik h₁ h₂ := ∀ o, lik h₁ o = lik h₂ o; readBoth is a likelihood under which heads and tails are not Tied (no theorem states ¬ Tied readBoth directly; it is used in seeking_turns_tails, where the posterior order turns, against seeking_keeps_tails under `agreeing`, which ties them).
rows.docstring: "**A model reading both tosses**: an outcome weighs its chance under the bias, in sixteenths"

rows.name: Agree.pickReading
rows.states: A choice of experiment as a function of the course so far: weight 1 for experiment true (the one using readBoth) and 0 for experiment false (the one using agreeing), whatever the course.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from List (Bool × (Bool × Bool)) × Bool to Nat (the `choose` argument of seekWeight).
rows.beside: It is the `choose` of seekWeight; seek_tied says that for any choose, a pair Tied under every experiment stays tied over every course (the choice weights depend only on the course). Used in seeking_turns_tails.
rows.docstring: "A policy choosing the experiment reading both tosses, whatever the course so far."

rows.name: Agree.readCourse
rows.states: A fixed course: one step, with experiment true chosen and outcome (true, true), two heads.
rows.shape: A LIST (one element) of LIST of (experiment Bool, outcome Bool × Bool).
rows.beside: none; a data constant named after the experiment it uses, the counterpart of agreeCourse; used in seeking_turns_tails.
rows.docstring: "One course of seeking: one step, the experiment reading both tosses, two heads."

rows.name: leftReading
rows.states: In the Routes example (three modes 0, 1, 2), the boolean value of a mode is true exactly when the mode is `zero`. It merges modes `one` and `two`. Together with the response leftRespond (route one on true, else route zero) it is Adequate: the route chosen from this boolean value arrives from every mode (left_adequate).
rows.shape: FUNCTION Mode (Fin 3) -> Bool, `decide (m = zero)`
rows.beside: No name without "read" in the module or its imports (Assurance, Witnesses). The relation it takes part in is `Adequate reading respond` (∀ m, the route `respond (reading m)` arrives from (m, false)), and coarsening is written inline as `∃ forget, ∀ m, q m = forget (p m)` (no_coarsest_adequate, common_coarsening_constant). Theorems: left_adequate, adequate_merges_outcomes, no_coarsest_adequate.
rows.docstring: Whether the mode is `zero`.

rows.name: rightReading
rows.states: In the Routes example, the boolean value of a mode is true exactly when the mode is `two`. It merges modes `zero` and `one`. With rightRespond (route zero on true, else route two) it is Adequate: the chosen route arrives from every mode (right_adequate). Any function of the mode that is a function of both leftReading and rightReading is constant (common_coarsening_constant).
rows.shape: FUNCTION Mode (Fin 3) -> Bool, `decide (m = two)`
rows.beside: none found. As for leftReading, the relations are the inline Adequate and the inline factoring `∃ forget, q m = forget (p m)`. Theorems: right_adequate, common_coarsening_inadequate, no_coarsest_adequate.
rows.docstring: Whether the mode is `two`.

rows.name: ActReadsWithin
rows.states: A premise on a family of exchange laws indexed by significance (act : (Pos → Nat → F → Prop) → ExchangeLaw F C). Take any two significances sig, sig' that agree (iff) at every position and step on every formation in `region`. Then at every step t, under every level history l, for every formation h with part h = true and every condition c that is coupled (obs) into some member of region, (act sig) and (act sig') have equal take and equal give at (t, h, l, c). In other words, on conditions coupled into the region, the part's act depends only on the significance's values on the region.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (act : (Pos → Nat → F → Prop) → ExchangeLaw F C, part : F → Bool, W : Web F C, obs : F → C → Prop, region : F → Prop)
rows.beside: No general named relation. It has the same shape as the `agree` premise of act_courses_unselected_throughout (take/give equal on conditions coupled into the closure), and significance_courses_unselected uses it, with region := WithinClosureOf (CoupledFromEither …) group, to supply that premise. Not tied to DependsOnlyOn or Sensitive by any theorem.
rows.docstring: A premise on how significance acts, not a law.

rows.name: ReadOffContinuations
rows.states: Take any two level histories l, l' such that, at every step t, every member g of `group` is admitted by the web at t under l exactly when it is admitted under l'. Then `select` holds at l exactly when it holds at l'. So the selection's value on a level history is fixed by the members' admissions at every step and by nothing else. No coupling or closure enters.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (W : Web F C, group : F → Prop, select : (Nat → C → Nat) → Prop)
rows.beside: It is Web.ReadOffCouplings with obs := thresholdOnly (readOffCouplings_thresholdOnly_iff). It implies ReadOffCouplings for every obs (ReadOffContinuations.couplings). Alike under all such selections ↔ admissions alike at every step (readOffContinuations_alike_iff). Web.ContinuationClass is an instance (continuationClass_reads, separates_continuations). Generic form: Learning.Training.Through (alike, select), with alike := admissions alike at every step, though no theorem ties the two.
rows.docstring: Histories admitting every member alike at every step are selected alike.

rows.name: ReadOffCouplings
rows.states: Take any two level histories l, l' that are Web.AlikeThrough obs g at every step t for every member g of `group`: admission of g alike, and the level of every condition c with obs g c equal. Then `select` holds at l exactly when it holds at l'. So the selection is invariant under changes that leave every member's admission and coupled-in levels unchanged over the whole run.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (W : Web F C, obs : F → C → Prop, group : F → Prop, select : (Nat → C → Nat) → Prop)
rows.beside: Web.SelectsThroughAll obs group t select (Selection.lean) is the up-to-step-t form. SelectsThroughAll.readOffCouplings and SelectsThrough.readOffCouplings give ReadOffCouplings from it. readOffCouplings_alike_iff: alike under every such selection ↔ ∀ member, ∀ t, AlikeThrough (from selects_alike_all_iff). readOffCouplings_alike_of_steps. Built on Web.AlikeThrough and AlikeThroughUpTo (Testing.lean). Also ReadOffCouplings.mono.
rows.docstring: A selection read off what couples into a group's members over the whole run: histories alike through every member's couplings at every step are selected alike.

rows.name: agentReads
rows.states: The projection of a four-part configuration onto its internal, sensory and active parts, as the triple (internal, sensory, active). In BlanketDetermined it is the map π of PartDependsOnlyOn P π agentParts: configurations equal on these three parts go, under one move, to configurations equal on the internal and active parts.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Parts I S A E -> I × S × A
rows.beside: It takes part in PartDependsOnlyOn P agentReads agentParts (the agent half of BlanketDetermined) and PartConsistentFamily H agentReads agentParts (BlanketConsistentFamily). Theorems: blanketed_determined, blanketed_step_alike, shownBy_blanketDetermined_iff, admitted_iff. PartDependsOnlyOn is the general relation, and it has DependsOnlyOn and GoAlike as its cases by definition. The projection itself has no other name.
rows.docstring: What the agent's next state reads: the internal, sensory and active parts.

rows.name: readFamily
rows.states: Given a map π : X → Parts I S A E and a family H of (state history, move history) pairs on X, this is the family on Parts that contains (g, m) exactly when some h with H h m satisfies g n = π (h n) at every step n. It is the pointwise image of the family under π, with the move histories kept.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (π : X → Parts I S A E) and (H : (Nat → X) → (Nat → M) → Prop) to a family (Nat → Parts I S A E) → (Nat → M) → Prop
rows.beside: none found (no image or map-of-family name elsewhere). Theorems about it: const_consistent, injective_consistent (π injective and BlanketConsistentFamily (readFamily π H) → ConsistentFamily H), whole_iff (BlanketConsistentFamily (readFamily whole H) ↔ ConsistentFamily H).
rows.docstring: A family read by `π`: the histories `π` makes of its histories, step by step.

rows.name: worldReads
rows.states: The projection of a four-part configuration onto its sensory, active and external parts, as the triple (sensory, active, external). In BlanketDetermined it is the map π of PartDependsOnlyOn P π worldParts: configurations equal on these three parts go, under one move, to configurations equal on the sensory and external parts.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Parts I S A E -> S × A × E
rows.beside: It takes part in PartDependsOnlyOn P worldReads worldParts (the world half of BlanketDetermined) and PartConsistentFamily H worldReads worldParts. Theorems: blanketed_determined, blanketed_step_alike, shownBy_partDependsOnlyOn_iff. The projection itself has no other name.
rows.docstring: What the world's next state reads: the sensory, active and external parts.

rows.name: ReadsOnlyActsFrom
rows.states: For a sequence of members acting in turn (Turns W O A), every member n ≥ k has a law whose value does not depend on its own coupling value. For all o, o' and every list `before` of earlier acts, law n o before = law n o' before. This holds on all inputs, including ones no run reaches.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (T : Turns W O A, k : Nat)
rows.beside: No named insensitivity relation is used. It is the negation, for all n ≥ k, of what separates_at characterises (law n giving different acts on two coupling values after the same earlier acts). With AlikeBefore k (couplings of members j < k equal), it gives acts_alike_of_cascade, act_alike_of_cascade and law_alike_of_cascade, and cascade_through: every select on the first N acts is Learning.Training.Through (AlikeBefore k).
rows.docstring: This is independence on all of the law's inputs, including histories no run reaches, not only on the runs that occur.

rows.name: read
rows.states: Two things carry this name. (1) In the general theorems (answer_alike_beyond_response, different_answers_not_beyond, answer_alike_beyond_law, and the Weighted section) it is a supplied variable: a function from a level history (Nat → C → Nat) to an optional yes/no answer. It always comes with the premise `through`: for any two histories l, l' that are alike through g's couplings at every step up to t (W.AlikeThroughUpTo obs g l l' t), the function gives the same answer. So it is an answer that depends only on what couples into g up to t. The theorems conclude that this answer is the same in both courses when g is outside the reach of the varying part. (2) In namespace Witness, `def read (l : Nat → Unit → Nat) : Option Bool := some (decide (0 < l 1 ()))` is concrete: the answer is `some true` exactly when the one condition's level at step 1 is positive, and `some false` otherwise.
rows.shape: (1) FUNCTION from level histories (Nat → C → Nat) to Option Bool, bound as a theorem argument and constrained by the premise `through`. In the Weighted section it is indexed by X, so its type is X → (Nat → C → Nat) → Option Bool. (2) FUNCTION (Nat → Unit → Nat) → Option Bool (Witness.read).
rows.beside: The relation the premise names is W.AlikeThroughUpTo (Testing.lean): the answer is constant on classes of histories alike through g's couplings up to t. No named predicate for "factors through AlikeThroughUpTo" exists in the module; the premise is spelled out in each theorem. For the witness, `Witness.read_through` proves that premise: on (web false), histories alike through `false`'s couplings up to step 1 give equal answers. `Witness.correct_answers` gives the two values.
rows.docstring: "Every response through a formation's complete past couplings agrees outside responsive reach." (on answer_alike_beyond_response; the def itself has no docstring)

rows.name: readOff
rows.states: A coupling-strength schedule built from the threshold world's own level. The strength at step u, on the level at step s, is 1 when s = u and the threshold world's level of its one condition at step u is at least θ. In every other case it is 0. It is Closing.Threshold.reading θ applied to the level history of thresholdWorld θ.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat → Bool → Unit → Nat → Unit → Nat (a strength schedule k u h c s d), with parameter θ : Nat
rows.beside: The schedule-maker it instantiates, Closing.Threshold.reading, satisfies Closing.ReadsBefore: the strengths at step t are equal for any two level histories that agree up to t (AgreeUpTo l l' t). That name is itself a "read" name; its read-free content is AgreeUpTo, and the theorem is Closing.Threshold.reads : ReadsBefore (reading θ). thresholdWorld_course states that the loop OnLoop … (strengthsBefore (θ+1) (readOff θ)) holds and the loop OnLoop … (strengthsBefore θ (readOff θ)) does not, so the loop forms at step θ. No read-free name for readOff itself.
rows.docstring: "The couplings the threshold world reads off its own standing."

rows.name: readJoint
rows.states: For a presentation p and two codes a, b: there is a configuration s such that p's relation holds for a with the probe `after s` and for b with the probe `before s`. Here p.read is the Presentation field of type C → Q → Prop, a relation between codes and probes. Decoded, it says that the fragment coded by a joins the idle fragment at s from the left, and the fragment coded by b joins it from the right.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on a Presentation (Fragment S A) (Probe S) C and two codes a b : C
rows.beside: The relation on fragments is Joint P f g, and the same condition stated on fragments is joint_iff_probes: Joint P f g ↔ ∃ s, probes P f (.after s) ∧ probes P g (.before s). readJoint_iff ties the two: when p is Exact for probes P, readJoint p (p.encode f) (p.encode g) ↔ Joint P f g. The field it uses, Presentation.read (Presentations.lean), is also a "read" name. Exact says p.read (p.encode m) q ↔ answers m q.
rows.docstring: "Joining read from codes: some configuration the first code joins before staying at and the second after."

rows.name: Frequency.readsLate
rows.states: A yes/no value for conditions d, c and steps n, m. It is true exactly when the following total is at least 1: over the steps s from 0 to m with n ≤ s, sum, over the formations h present at m and outside the part, the strength k m h c s d. Put plainly: at step m, some present formation outside the part exchanges with c, with positive strength, on the level of d at some step s with n ≤ s ≤ m.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (part, k, present, d, c, n, m) → Bool; a decidable two-place family in n, m for fixed d, c
rows.beside: It is the decision of ∃ s, n ≤ s ∧ CouplesAt cs part k present m s d c (CouplesAt, Remainder.lean). Two theorems tie them. Frequency.readsLate_of_couplesAt gives CouplesAt … m s d c with n ≤ s → readsLate … = true. Frequency.couplesAt_of_readsLate gives the converse when every condition is listed (∀ c, c ∈ cs). It is used in recurs_or_stops, which links it to CouplingRecurs and StopsBy.
rows.docstring: "**Whether a late level is read at a step.** At step `m` a formation present, outside the part, exchanges with `c` with positive strength on a level of `d` at a step from `n` on."

rows.name: byReading
rows.states: The dependence sense does not apply here: the name is a decision policy. For each candidate c it gives the move `off` when gain c < loss c, and `go` otherwise, including when they are equal. It is byRule applied to the test gain c < loss c. "Reading" names the off-switch literature's human, who knows the candidate. It does not name a relation of dependence.
rows.shape: FUNCTION C → Move, parameterised by gain loss : C → Nat
rows.beside: Read-free name: byRule (fun c => decide (gain c < loss c)); byReading is defined as exactly that, so it holds by rfl. Theorems: byReading_of_lt, byReading_of_not_lt and byReading_best (it is BestAt [go, off] (shifted gain loss) at each candidate). Also shortfall_byReading and after_byReading.
rows.docstring: "**The policy after a reading that tells the candidate and stops by the supplied values**: it stops exactly where the loss exceeds the gain, and goes on where they are equal"

rows.name: Reads
rows.states: For a law next and places q, k: some hexagram s exists for which flipping the line at q changes the line at k of the next hexagram, (next (flip q s)).line k ≠ (next s).line k. So line k of the next configuration is not fixed independently of line q of the present one: changing q alone can change it. The direction runs from line q of the present configuration to line k of the next.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (next : Hexagram → Hexagram) and two places q k : Place
rows.beside: It is the failure of Learning.Lumped for any map blind to place q. runsOrder_blind_not_lumped turns runsOrder_reads (Reads next q k for every q, k when next runs the received order) into ¬ Learning.Lumped π (fun s => (next s).line k) for every π with π (flip q s) = π s. It has the same shape as ExchangeLaw.Sensitive in Counterfactual.lean (changing c's levels alone changes h's exchange), but no theorem ties the two.
rows.docstring: "The line at `k` of the next configuration reads the line at `q`: at some configuration, changing the line at `q` changes the line at `k` of the next."

rows.name: readsb
rows.states: A decidable check on a list of hexagrams. It is true when two consecutive pairs (st, st') of the list exist such that the first member of st' is the first member of st with line q flipped, and the second members of the two pairs differ at line k. It gives a witness inside the list that line k of the successor changes when line q of the present hexagram is flipped.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (List Hexagram, Place, Place) → Bool
rows.beside: Tied to Reads in one direction only. reads_of_readsb: if Follows next l and readsb l q k = true, then Reads next q k. runsOrder_reads uses it with the received order. No converse theorem exists.
rows.docstring: "Two steps of a list, the second from the first's start changed at `q`, going on to lines that differ at `k`, told step by step."

rows.name: Flow.readAt
rows.states: Reindexes a flow by a function of steps σ. At step s, the new flow's present list, takings and givings are those of L at step σ s. It is precomposition with σ. Nothing is summed or merged.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (Flow F C, Nat → Nat) → Flow F C
rows.beside: Its counterpart for webs is Web.sample (Sampling.lean), which reindexes in the same way: level, active, requires, need and draws are taken at σ s. It is not Flow.sample (Sampling.lean): that one sums over each span of fine steps. No theorem ties readAt to Flow.sample. It is used in World.withoutIdle (v.flow.readAt σ with v.web.sample σ). withoutIdle_sameAt shows that each step n of the world matches step σ (ρ n), relatum by relatum (Web.SameAt). Also see withoutIdle_premises and withoutIdle_totals.
rows.docstring: "A flow read at the steps `σ`: across step `s` the exchange across step `σ s`."

rows.name: Reading
rows.states: Reading π f k v holds where some configuration s has π s = k and f s = v: the relation, from a reduced value k to a value v, that pairs k with every value f takes on the configurations π sends to k. It is the image of f's graph pushed along π; it gives at most one v per k exactly where f goes alike across configurations π merges.
rows.shape: PREDICATE (a relation K → V → Prop) built from π : S → K and f : S → V; defined as ∃ s, π s = k ∧ f s = v.
rows.beside: Learning.Lumped π f (Learning.lean:834: π i = π i' → f i = f i'). Tied by Readout.reading_single_iff: SingleValued (Reading π f) ↔ Lumped π f. Also Readout.Decodes π f g (f s = g (π s)), with lumped_of_decodes. Lumped is the same 'goes alike across what π merges' relation that Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn / Laws.GoAlike state for a Process's step; no theorem here ties Reading to those directly.
rows.docstring: What `f` reads through `π`: `f` takes the value `v` at some configuration `π` sends to `k`.

rows.name: ReadsDirectly
rows.states: Given part : S → (p : P) → G p, a family read : (c : C) → S → W c and an assignment use : P → C, it holds where, for every part p and configurations s, s', equal values of the function read (use p) at s and s' force equal part p at s and s'. Direction: agreement under the assigned function determines agreement at the part (the function separates whatever that part separates); the converse direction is ThroughParts.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (part, read, use): ∀ p s s', read (use p) s = read (use p) s' → part s p = part s' p. The argument named `read` is just a C-indexed family of functions on S.
rows.beside: Readout.ThroughParts part read (∀ c s s', (∀ p, part s p = part s' p) → read c s = read c s': each function depends only on the parts, i.e. a DependsOnlyOn/Lumped-shaped condition). Tied by Readout.agree_iff_parts: under ThroughParts and ReadsDirectly, (∀ c, read c s = read c s') ↔ ∀ p, part s p = part s' p; and supplied_agree_iff_parts. Unrelated homonym: BlanketWeights.lean has a namespace ReadsDirectly holding an example rate (rate depends on the external bit, `reads_external`), not this predicate.
rows.docstring: `use p` reads part `p` directly: configurations it reads alike agree at that part.

rows.name: survivingReads
rows.states: A worked-example value, not a relation: the assignment from domains to optional observations that gives nothing at domains d < 2 (the two members sharing a cause) and, at every other domain, the observation of the renewed installation at the root address (its epoch, serial, address [] and the key located there). It is passed to Transactions.guardedExecute with survivingApprovals in repaired_completes.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Domain → Option Observation (type Transactions.Readings), a concrete definition.
rows.beside: Transactions.Readings := Domain → Option Observation; Transactions.observed w address (the Observation an installation gives at an address); Transactions.faithfulReads w p (every domain gives observed w p.address); Transactions.readSupport p reports d (domain d's entry equals what request p expects). No relational name of the DependsOnlyOn kind applies; no theorem ties survivingReads to faithfulReads.
rows.docstring: Readings of the members outside the shared cause.

rows.name: ReadsPointwise
rows.states: For a law f from states (ι → Nat) to states, it holds where two states equal at every condition j are sent to states equal at every condition i. It says f's output at each condition is the same for any two inputs that agree at every condition. Note: with funext (which rests on the Quot.sound axiom) every f satisfies it; the module states it as a premise because it keeps an empty axiom report, and proves it from KeepsBelow by antisymmetry.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on f : (ι → Nat) → (ι → Nat): ∀ x y, (∀ j, x j = y j) → ∀ i, f x i = f y i.
rows.beside: Same shape as RegimeMargin.Pointwise G (each giving G i returns the same for inputs equal at every condition) and RegimeMargin.respects. Tied by pointwise_step (Pointwise G → ReadsPointwise (step Drawn.whole G H)), reads_of_keepsBelow (KeepsBelow f → ReadsPointwise f), and used by run_alike_of (runs from states equal at every condition stay equal at every condition), stays_at, repeats, ends_iff_within, ending_iff. It is a DependsOnlyOn/Lumped-shaped condition with π the pointwise-equality relation; no theorem ties it to Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn by name.
rows.docstring: **A law of states reads them condition by condition**: states alike at every condition go to states alike at every condition.

rows.name: ReadsLate
rows.states: For a delay ℓ and a rule ρ (from the rest's record of give/take pairs to the regulator's give/take at each step), it holds where, at every step t, what ρ gives and takes is the same for any two records that agree at every step s with s + ℓ < t. ρ's answer at t depends only on the record up to step t − ℓ − 1.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (ℓ : Nat, ρ : Rule), Rule := Record → Nat → Nat × Nat, Record := Nat → Nat × Nat: ∀ δ δ' t, (∀ s, s + ℓ < t → δ s = δ' s) → ρ δ t = ρ δ' t.
rows.beside: Closest named relation: Testing.AlikeThroughUpTo (levels alike through a step), and in shape a time-delayed DependsOnlyOn; no theorem in Regulation ties ReadsLate to either. Its own consequences: ReadsLate.alike (records agreeing before T give the same answer at every step up to T + ℓ), late_spread, late_band, no_narrower_band (the least band is 2(ℓ+1)d), levels_alike; lateReturn_readsLate gives a rule satisfying it.
rows.docstring: **The rule reads `ℓ` steps late.** What it gives and takes at step `t` is the same for two records of the rest that agree at every step `s` with `s + ℓ < t`: the steps whose effect on the level shows by the level at `t - ℓ`.

rows.name: read
rows.states: In namespace Revising: for a state s = (stock, link, response) and an alternative b : Bool, it returns b where the link coordinate s.2.1 is true and false otherwise. So the built link makes the two alternatives give different values; without it both give false. It is used only to define Revising.alike s b c := read s b = read s c, the lumping of alternatives at state s.
rows.shape: FUNCTION State → Bool → Bool (State := Nat × Bool × Bool).
rows.beside: Revising.alike (defined from it), used as the lumping in Registration.Keeps alike s t (every pair alike at t is alike at s) and Registration.AlikeUpTo; Learning.Training.Through. RevisionRuns has a theorem with conclusion Registration.Keeps Revising.alike s t where s.2 = (false, false) (around line 430). No theorem ties read itself to DependsOnlyOn or Lumped.
rows.docstring: The built link separates two represented alternatives.

rows.name: reading
rows.states: The rule on candidates that returns true at candidate c exactly where gain c < offGain c (switching the law off at c gains more than keeping it). Put into held weight r a, it gives the plan that switches off at the weight of the candidates where it returns true and keeps at the others.
rows.shape: FUNCTION C → Bool: fun c => decide (gain c < offGain c).
rows.beside: No relational name. It is one instance of the rule argument r : C → Bool of RevisionPlans.held; theorems about it: excess_reading (held weight (reading gain offGain) a has excess 0), the balance theorems (above_iff, not_above_iff), and the hold/evade examples (hold_four_below).
rows.docstring: **The reading that tells the candidate**: it stops exactly where switching off gains more than keeping.

rows.name: routeRead
rows.states: The end value of a route point: 0 at a level point (.level τ c) and 1 at the source. Summed by counting.transfer over the route weights, it makes routeSum the total weight of the courses that end at a source.
rows.shape: FUNCTION RoutePoint C → Nat, defined by cases.
rows.beside: No relational name; it is the end-value argument of counting.transfer / counting.along in routeSum (Routes.lean) and in CourseWorlds.lean:429. Weights.sum_courses expands the transfer it feeds.
rows.docstring: What is read at the end of a course: whether it has reached a source.

rows.name: Unread
rows.states: For a two-level step on pairs (a, b) (a the share, b what lies beyond it) with a fast update f and a rule update h: the share component of f((a,b), g) is the same for any two b, b' with the same a and rule g, and h((a,b), g) is the same for any two b, b'. That is, the next share and the next rule depend only on the share and the current rule, not on b. Body: (∀ a b b' g, (f (a, b) g).1 = (f (a, b') g).1) ∧ ∀ a b b' g, h (a, b) g = h (a, b') g.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on a pair of functions f : A × B → R → A × B and h : A × B → R → R.
rows.beside: Same relation as GoAlike (Laws.lean) of the two-level process Pace.step f h reads under the projection loopPart (share, rule, step count). Tied by goAlike_of_unread (Unread → GoAlike for every schedule), identifiesAlike_iff_unread (IdentifiesAlike of loopPart along every schedule ↔ Unread), courses_alike_iff_unread (courses from starts with equal share and rule have equal share and rule at every step, along every schedule ↔ Unread), unread_course and reads_beyond_of_apart (¬Unread from a step where such courses differ). Close in kind to DependsOnlyOn (Mechanism.lean, not imported here); no theorem ties them directly. A relational name would be 'the share-and-rule part does not depend on B'.
rows.docstring: **Neither the share's next value nor the rule read reads what lies beyond the share.**

rows.name: joinRead
rows.states: Given a rule update hA : A → R → R defined on the share alone, joinRead hA is the rule update on pairs that applies hA to the first component and ignores the second: joinRead hA (a, b) g = hA a g. It lifts a share-only rule update to the pair (share, what lies beyond).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (A → R → R) to (A × B → R → R).
rows.beside: join_unread: Unread (join fA fB) (joinRead hA), i.e. the lifted update does not depend on B by construction; turn_join and join_course: the joined course equals the share's own course on share and rule. No relation-named counterpart; the name could be 'the share's rule update, lifted to the pair'.
rows.docstring: The share's reading, read on the pair.

rows.name: closedRead
rows.states: In the witness Beyond: the rule update that returns the rule hi (carriers four offspring to each other's one) whatever the share and whatever the current rule: closedRead _ _ = hi. It depends on nothing.
rows.shape: FUNCTION CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts (constant).
rows.beside: Used as joinRead closedRead, so Unread holds via join_unread. closed_locked: the course under it has loss ≥ t at step t, is Locked at every step, and the share never falls below twoToOne. Note the word is doubly off: this update does not depend on the share either; it is constant. A relational name: 'the constant rule hi'.
rows.docstring: Read from the share alone: favouring the carriers four to one at every share.

rows.name: lossRead
rows.states: In the witness Beyond: the rule update on (share, loss) pairs that returns hi while the loss p.2 is below 1 and lo (others four to one) once the loss is at least 1, ignoring the share and the current rule. So the next rule depends on the loss, which lies beyond the share.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (CarrierCounts × Nat) → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts.
rows.beside: open_reads: ¬ Unread (join select lossStep) lossRead (two starts equal in share and rule, losses 0 and 1, give different rules at step 1, via reads_beyond_of_apart). lossRead_turns: from loss ≥ 1 the returned rule does not favour the carriers. open_turned, open_falls. Relational name: 'the rule as a function of the loss (threshold 1)'; the relation is 'the next rule depends on the loss', i.e. ¬Unread.
rows.docstring: Read from the loss: favouring the carriers while the loss is below one, the others after.

rows.name: read
rows.states: Two uses. (1) In section Readers it is a variable read : Q → S → G → G: the function giving the next rule from a second-level state q (called 'the reading'), the share x and the current rule g. (2) In namespace Proportional it is the def read q _ _ := q: the next rule is the second-level state q itself, ignoring share and current rule.
rows.shape: (1) FUNCTION variable Q → S → G → G; (2) FUNCTION CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts (projection onto the first argument).
rows.beside: readMono (Proportional): monotone in q and x. Enters ReadsShare (RuleCapture.lean: the rule update is monotone in the share alone) through both_reads: monotone read and monotone mind give ReadsShare P (both MG MQ) (readers read mind). No relation-named counterpart; a plain name would be 'rule from state' (1) or 'the rule is the state' (2).
rows.docstring: The rule read is the reading.

rows.name: readers
rows.states: Given read : Q → S → G → G and mind : S → Q → Q, readers read mind is the rule update on pairs (rule g, state q): at share x it first forms the new state q' = mind x q, then the new rule read q' x g, and returns (read (mind x q) x g, mind x q). It composes a state update from the share with a rule update from the new state and the share into one update of the pair. Also used as the name of hypotheses order.le v u / order.le u v in Drawn (pool_mono, pool_against, pool_reads, pool_through): there it names the premise that the carriers' weight vector u is at least / at most the others' v in the ratio order.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (Q → S → G → G) → (S → Q → Q) → S → G × Q → G × Q (the def); and a hypothesis name of type order.le v u (a PROPOSITION comparing two CarrierCounts).
rows.beside: both_reads: ReadsShare P (both MG MQ) (readers read mind) under monotonicity of read and mind, i.e. the paired update is monotone in the share alone; then readers_not_below, reading_absorbed, readers_uniform_locks carry RuleCapture's lock laws to the pair. No relation-named counterpart; a plain name would be 'the paired update (state, then rule)'.
rows.docstring: **The reading read from the share**: at a reading step the reading is formed from the share (`mind`), and the rule is read from the share through the reading so formed (`read`).

rows.name: poolRead
rows.states: In namespace Drawn: poolRead u v x _ := pool u v x, the rule update that ignores the current rule and returns the pool of the population x with weight vectors u (each carrier's) and v (each other's): carrier part x.carrier*u.carrier + x.other*v.carrier, other part x.carrier*u.other + x.other*v.other. The next rule is a population-weighted sum of two fixed rules.
rows.shape: FUNCTION CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts → CarrierCounts (the last argument, the current rule, unused).
rows.beside: pool_reads_iff: ReadsShare order order (poolRead u v) ↔ order.le v u (the update is monotone in the share exactly where u favours carriers at least as much as v); pool_reads, pool_against (antitone where u ≤ v), pool_through, pool_not_rising, through_locks. Relational name: 'the population-weighted pool of u and v'.
rows.docstring: The pool read at a reading step, from the population alone.

rows.name: ReadsBefore
rows.states: For a strength law κ that takes a level history l and gives coupling strengths κ l t h c s d: for every step t, any two level histories l, l' that agree at every step up to t (AgreeUpTo l l' t) give the same strengths at t for every formation h, condition c, earlier step s and condition d. The strengths at t depend only on the levels up to t.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on κ : (Nat → C → Nat) → Nat → F → C → Nat → C → Nat.
rows.beside: The same shape as ExchangeLaw.Nonanticipating (Counterfactual.lean: the law gives alike under histories that AgreeUpTo t), applied to the strengths rather than to the law. Tied by ExchangeLaw.carryingRead_nonanticipating: ReadsBefore κ → (ExchangeLaw.carryingRead cs part σ κ).Nonanticipating. Relational name: 'κ is nonanticipating' / 'κ at t depends only on levels up to t'.
rows.docstring: **Strengths read from the levels so far.** At each step the strengths depend on the levels up to that step only.

rows.name: ExchangeLaw.carryingRead
rows.states: The exchange law that takes nothing and, at step t, has formation h give condition c the amount carriedGive cs part σ (κ l) t h c l: σ t h c if h is in the part, otherwise the sum over earlier steps s ≤ t and listed conditions d of the strength κ l t h c s d times the level l s d. It is ExchangeLaw.carrying (Propagation.lean) with the fixed strengths k replaced by strengths κ l computed from the level history itself.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (cs : List C, part : F → Bool, σ, κ) to ExchangeLaw F C (a structure with take and give).
rows.beside: ExchangeLaw.carrying (Propagation.lean) is the fixed-strength version. formedCourse_eq_carried: under ReadsBefore κ, the course it generates (formedCourse) equals carried cs part σ (κ (formedCourse …)) …, the carrying law's course with the strengths the course itself produces. carryingRead_nonanticipating ties it to Nonanticipating. Relational name: 'the carrying law with history-dependent strengths'.
rows.docstring: **The carrying law with read strengths.** The part gives its gaps, each formation outside it what the strengths read from the levels make of them, and nothing is taken.

rows.name: reading
rows.states: In Closing.Threshold: the strength law with one condition: for level history l, step u, formation h, condition c, earlier step s and condition d, the strength is 1 if s = u and the level at u has reached θ (θ ≤ l u ()), else 0. The exchange into the one condition responds to its current level once that level is at least θ.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat → (Nat → Unit → Nat) → Nat → Bool → Unit → Nat → Unit → Nat (θ, then a strength law κ).
rows.beside: reads θ : ReadsBefore (reading θ), i.e. its strengths at u depend only on the level at u. Feeds level, strengths, level_succ, forms, not_formed, unforeseen. Relational name: 'the threshold coupling at θ' (the strength from the current level, switched on at θ).
rows.docstring: The exchange of the formation outside the part with the one condition responds to its current level once that level has reached `θ`.

rows.name: readEvidence
rows.states: A parsing function on record lists: a list of exactly three records (x, y, z) is mapped to some Evidence ⟨a, b, xs⟩ where a is the single value of x if x is a record of probe p0, b the single value of y if y is a record of p1, xs the values of z if z is a record of orderProbe; every other list (lengths 0, 1, 2, 4+, or wrong expressions or value counts) maps to none. Not a dependence relation: here 'read' means decode or parse.
rows.shape: FUNCTION List (Expr × List Bool) → Option Evidence.
rows.beside: records_supply_evidence: readEvidence (trialRecords c) = some (observe c), i.e. decoding the three probe records of c gives c's probe values (decoding is a left inverse of record-making on these lists); used in interpretationFromRecords and step_evidence. Not about dependence; a plain name would be 'parseEvidence' or 'evidenceOfRecords'.
rows.docstring: The probes read off three records in probe order, or none.

rows.name: readings
rows.states: The list of the values val(state t) of a run for t = n-1 down to 0: the first n configurations of the run each mapped through val : σ → C → Bool to a valuation of the claims C, latest first. Body: Learning.prefixOf (Parting.course val r) n, where Parting.course val r = fun t => val (r.state t). 'Reading' here means one value of the map val, i.e. a valuation C → Bool assigned to a configuration; nothing about dependence.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (abbrev) from a map val : σ → C → Bool, a run r : Run P and n : Nat to a LIST of valuations (C → Bool) of length n.
rows.beside: Same object without 'read': Parting.course val r (the course of a run through a map) and Learning.prefixOf (prefix of a course, latest first); readings is literally prefixOf (course val r) n, so they are tied by definition (abbrev), no separate theorem. The same module's `passes val r` (the set of valuations v with ∃ t, val (r.state t) = v) is the whole-run counterpart; no theorem ties passes to readings directly. No DependsOnlyOn/Sensitive analogue applies.
rows.docstring: The context-free readings of the first `n` configurations of a run, the latest first.

rows.name: ReadsAdjacent
rows.states: For a relation rel on relata R, a list us and a law of levels law : (R → Nat) → R → Nat: for every listed relatum x and any two configurations a, b, if a x = b x and a y = b y at every listed y adjacent to x under rel, then law a x = law b x. That is, the law's next level at x is the same for any two configurations that agree at x and at its listed neighbours: the next level at x depends only on the levels at x and its adjacent listed relata (a locality condition on the law).
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (rel : R → R → Bool, us : List R, law : (R → Nat) → R → Nat).
rows.beside: It is a per-relatum, neighbourhood form of Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn (P π: two configurations alike under π step to one configuration), but stated for a function law and a neighbourhood projection at each x; Continuity does not import or name DependsOnlyOn for it, and no theorem ties them. Used with Conserves in conservedOn_of_law and balancesOn_of_law (local conservation from global). The instance `reads : ReadsAdjacent together all swap` shows the two-relatum swap meets it.
rows.docstring: A law of levels reads only adjacent relata: its next level at a listed relatum is the same from two configurations that agree there and at every listed relatum adjacent to it.

rows.name: Reads
rows.states: For a site map read : Nat → Option α, a starting index i and a word x0 :: x1 :: ...: read i = some x0, read (i+1) = some x1, and so on for every token of the word (True for the empty word). That is, the given site map supplies exactly the word's tokens at consecutive sites starting at i; it is agreement of a function Nat → Option α with a list on an index window.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (read : Nat → Option α, i : Nat, word : List α), defined by recursion on the list.
rows.beside: No name without 'read' for this relation in Copying or Gated. Tied to readSteps by Copying.reading_iff: n = word.length steps of readSteps produce built ++ word exactly when Reads read built.length word ∧ Supplies word pool ∧ use draw prev word ≤ free.
rows.docstring: The site `i` of a word read through `read`: each site reads the word's token.

rows.name: readStep
rows.states: A function from a copy-in-progress s : Scan α and an optional token o to the next Scan: if o = none, or nothing is pending, s is unchanged; if o = some x and a token is pending, x is attached (appended to built, removed from the pool, draw s.previous x moved from free to used) provided the pool holds x and the free support covers draw s.previous x; otherwise s is unchanged. It is the module's tick (one move of the copy) with the attached token supplied from outside (o) instead of taken from the head of pending; the pending head is dropped regardless of whether it equals x.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Scan α and Option α to Scan α (parameterised by draw : Option α → α → Nat).
rows.beside: Copying.tick is the same move with the token taken from s.pending's head; no theorem in the module ties readStep to tick. readStep_extends states its product only grows (∃ tail, built' = built ++ tail).
rows.docstring: One move of a copy attaching what the reading gives at the next site, given that reading.

rows.name: readSteps
rows.states: n-fold iteration of readTick: readSteps read 0 s = s, readSteps read (n+1) s = readSteps read n (readTick read s). The state of the copy after n moves in which each attached token is the value of the site map read at the current length of the product.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from a site map (Nat → Option α), a count n : Nat and Scan α to Scan α.
rows.beside: Copying.steps is the same iteration of tick (token from pending). No theorem ties readSteps to steps. Theorems: readSteps_fixed (a fixed point of readTick stays fixed), readSteps_extends (product only grows), reading_iff (ties readSteps to Reads, Supplies and use).
rows.docstring: `n` moves of a copy reading through `read`.

rows.name: readTick
rows.states: readTick read s = readStep s (read s.built.length): one move of the copy in which the token offered for attachment is the value of the site map read at index equal to the current length of the product built. So the token attached at site i is a function of i through read, not of the pending list.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from a site map (Nat → Option α) and Scan α to Scan α.
rows.beside: Copying.tick is the counterpart with the token from s.pending; no tying theorem. readSteps iterates it.
rows.docstring: One move of a copy reading through `read`: the token attached at site `i` is what `read` reads at `i`.

rows.name: ReadsCountByCount
rows.states: For a rule : M → (F → V) → (F → V) → F → V: for every m, and count vectors c, c', d, d', if c w = c' w and d w = d' w at every word w, then rule m c d w = rule m c' d' w at every w. It is pointwise extensionality of the rule in its two count arguments (the result depends on the counts only through their values word by word), stated because funext is not used; the docstring says it restricts nothing else.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on rule : M → (F → V) → (F → V) → F → V.
rows.beside: No relational name in the module or imports for this extensionality (it is the pointwise-congruence form of a function's dependence on its arguments, not DependsOnlyOn on a process). Used together with CommutesWithRenaming in hear_keeps and tied_hears_tied; no theorem ties it to another name.
rows.docstring: The rule reads the counts count by count: counts that agree at every word give one result.

rows.name: reread
rows.states: Not about dependence. A function giving the State after drawing ticket.1.length + 1 units: reserve minus (length+1), time plus (length+1), drawn plus (length+1). It is the cost of checking the found route's address again in the current tree before acting ('re-read' = an operational recheck, a cost charge).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Ticket and State to State.
rows.beside: It equals the result of Actuation.draw (length+1) (length+1) s where draw succeeds; used via draw_some in dispatch_completes. Not part of the read-as-dependence family.
rows.docstring: The state after the re-read's draw.

rows.name: drawnRead
rows.states: The rule-update map for the paced two-level course: drawnRead a p c hi lo pos x g = drawn a p c hi lo pos x, i.e. the new rule at an update step is the pool (ClosedCapture.Drawn.pool) of the two shaped rules RuleShaping.shaped a hi p c and shaped a lo p c, each weighted as the population x counts its carriers and others; the second argument (the current rule g) is ignored. So the updated rule is a function of the population x alone. In Pace.turn it is applied at steps where the schedule `reads` is true; elsewhere the rule is kept.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from CarrierCounts × CarrierCounts (population, current rule, the latter unused) to CarrierCounts; plays the role h : S → R → R in Pace.paced.
rows.beside: The relational name for its property is RuleCapture.ReadsShare (h is monotone in the population/share alone: P.le x y → M.le (h x g) (h y g')), itself containing 'read'. Tied by DrawnShaping.drawn_reads_iff: ReadsShare order order (drawnRead …) ↔ lo ≤ hi, and drawn_against (hi ≤ lo gives ReadsShare against the reversed order). Also feeds Locked in the lock theorems.
rows.docstring: The rule read at a reading step, from the population alone.

rows.name: readWeb
rows.states: ExchangeRelation.readWeb L l need is the Web built by Flow.readOff from a flow L and level history l: level = l, active = L.Exchanging (a formation is active exactly where it exchanges), draws f c = 0 < L.take t f c, need = need, and requires t f c = RespondsBelow l t f c (need t f c): under every history differing from l at most in c's level at t, with that level below the need, no exchange the relation admits has f exchange. So 'requires' is defined as necessary non-exchange of f when c's level is changed alone to fall below the need (a counterfactual dependence of f's exchange on c's level), and the rest of the web is copied from the flow.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from a flow L : Flow F C, a level history l : Nat → C → Nat and need : Nat → F → C → Nat to a Web F C (a structure with fields level, active, requires, need, draws); defined in namespace ExchangeRelation (parallel ExchangeLaw.readWeb in Reading.lean for a law's course).
rows.beside: Flow.readOff (Reading.lean) is the construction; RespondsBelow is the relation it puts into `requires`. readWeb_dependent: on every run (rel.Runs present l L) the web is Dependent. relation_readWeb_requires ties the relation's web over the law's course to ExchangeLaw.readWeb; relation_readWeb_may ties it to MayRespondBelow. Counterfactual.ExchangeLaw.Sensitive (changing c's levels alone changes h's exchange at some step) is a nearby relation, but no theorem ties it to readWeb or RespondsBelow.
rows.docstring: The web read off a run: activity and drawing read off its exchange, the levels the history's, and a formation requiring a condition at its need exactly where its exchange necessarily responds to the condition falling below that need.

rows.name: read
rows.states: Not a knower-known relation: an arithmetic replenishment. read m k l is the level after k units each add one unit to the level l while it is below the set level m: if l < m it is min(l + k, m), otherwise l is unchanged. In step it is applied only when the supply is on, with k the number of units present (x.ages.length) and l the level after the draw.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat (set level m, count of units k, level l) to the new level
rows.beside: none found: no dependence name applies, this is a capped addition (min(l + k, m) below m). Its only law here is read_pos (1 ≤ m and 1 ≤ k give 1 ≤ read m k l). A plain name would be 'replenish' or 'intake'.
rows.docstring: The read: `k` units, in turn, each take one while the level is below `m`.

rows.name: reader (what a reader is in this module)
rows.states: The 'reader' is the list of units with their ages (field St.ages : List Nat) that draw from the supply into the level; it is present where that list is non-empty (Present x := x.ages ≠ []). Units age by one a step and end at the span s; where fewer than n remain, one new unit is made from the rule's Source (given, supply, level, none). It is a regenerating constraint holding a stock, not anything facing an object.
rows.shape: STRUCTURE FIELD St.ages : List Nat (ages of units); PREDICATE Present on St; the rebuild source is the inductive Source
rows.beside: The region where the units are present is shown closed under the supplied step with «闭» (GrammarLaws): theorem «供则读者之域闭» : «闭» (supplied r) Present; the emptied state is «闭» under the net (theorem «取于储者绝而不复»). The family law «以储买时当且仅当取于储» : BuysTime r ↔ r.source = .level. No dependence-relation name.
rows.docstring: An occurrence: the level, and the reader's units by age.

rows.name: Flow.readOff
rows.states: Given a flow L and supplied levels, requirements and needs, builds the web whose activity is L.Exchanging (f is present at t and takes or gives a positive amount of some condition) and whose drawing relation is 'L.take t f c > 0'. So a formation is active exactly where it exchanges and draws on exactly the conditions it takes from; levels, requirements and needs pass through unchanged.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from a Flow F C plus (level : Nat → C → Nat, requires : Nat → F → C → Prop, need : Nat → F → C → Nat) to a Web F C (a constructor filling Web's fields)
rows.beside: Activity is Flow.Exchanging (same module); ties: readOff_acting (L.Acting of it), readOff_taking (L.Taking of it), and acting_taking_iff_wider: for any web W, L.Acting W ∧ L.Taking W ↔ every Exchanging f is W.active and every positive take is W.draws. Not a dependence relation; a 'web derived from the exchange'.
rows.docstring: The web read off the exchange: the levels, requirements and needs given, a formation active exactly where it exchanges, and drawing on exactly what it takes from.

rows.name: ExchangeLaw.readWeb
rows.states: The web derived from the course a law of exchange generates from a start: activity and drawing as in Flow.readOff applied to law.course, levels law.levels, and f requires c at need n exactly where RespondsBelow holds: under every level history that differs from the generated one at most in c's level at step t, with that level below n, f does not exchange across t. So requirement is a counterfactual dependence of f's exchange on c's level, not a fact of the course (requirement_beyond_course: two laws with one identical course give opposite requirements).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from an ExchangeLaw F C, present : Nat → List F, start : C → Nat, need : Nat → F → C → Nat to a Web F C
rows.beside: Requirement slot is ExchangeLaw.RespondsBelow (same module). Closest dependence names: Counterfactual.Sensitive / InsensitiveAt (c's levels alone change h's exchange at some step); no theorem ties RespondsBelow to Sensitive found. ExchangePremises.lean has ExchangeRelation.readWeb (requirement as necessary response over an admitted relation) tied by ExchangeLaw.relation_readWeb_requires and relation_readWeb_may. Laws here: supported_of_responds (exchanging and responding give n ≤ l t c), readWeb_dependent, reading_glue.
rows.docstring: The web read off the course the law generates: activity and drawing read off its exchange, and a formation requiring a condition at its need exactly where its exchange responds to the condition falling below that need.

rows.name: ExchangeLaw.readWorld
rows.states: The World whose relata are of one type R, whose flow is the course the law generates from start, and whose web is ExchangeLaw.readWeb of that course (activity = exchanging, drawing = positive take, requirement = RespondsBelow at the given need).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from ExchangeLaw R R, present, start, need to World (World.of R (law.course …) (law.readWeb …))
rows.beside: Ties: readWorld_glue (with the rest counted: Balanced, Acting, Taking, Dependent hold with no premise); readWorld_closed_iff (for a Nonanticipating law, the rest is never active ↔ law.Feasible). Nonanticipating is defined via GivesAlike/AgreeUpTo in Counterfactual (exchange at t depends only on levels up to t).
rows.docstring: The course a law generates over one kind of relatum, read as a world with activity, drawing and requirement read off the law.

rows.name: Unread
rows.states: For a schedule s : Nat → X (which condition is attended at each step), x is not the scheduled condition at any of the k steps from T: for all j < k, s (T + j) ≠ x. A gap of length k in the schedule's visits to x.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (s : Nat → X, x : X, T k : Nat)
rows.beside: Its complement in windows is Within s x a (every stretch of a steps contains a step with s = x). Tied by within_iff: Within s x a ↔ ∀ T, ¬ Unread s x T a (equality decided), and Within.unread_lt, read_or_unread. Used in Flow.Balances.loses_of_unread (a gap lets a part withdrawn late draw (k+1+ℓ)d). Homonym, different relation: ClosedCapture.Unread f h (the share's next value and the rule do not depend on what lies beyond the share), tied to GoAlike by ClosedCapture.goAlike_of_unread.
rows.docstring: The schedule `s` leaves `x` unread for the `k` steps from `T`.

rows.name: Code.reader
rows.states: The schedule a binary code generates: the function giving, at each step, which condition (if any) the code visits. idle gives none at every step, leaf x gives some x at every step, node l r alternates steps between the two branches' schedules (weave: even steps l, odd steps r).
rows.shape: FUNCTION Code X → (Nat → Option X)
rows.beside: none found as a dependence name; it is a schedule. Tied to Within by Code.At.reads: a condition at depth k is visited within every 2^k steps (Within K.reader (some x) (2^k)); kraft_reads and half_suffices build on it.
rows.docstring: What a code reads at each step.

rows.name: ChangeReading
rows.states: A two-element index type naming the two ways a condition's change across a step is computed: standing (from the level before and after) and exchange (from what the flow gave and took). It is a label, a 'context' index of a Contextual system, not a relation.
rows.shape: INDUCTIVE TYPE with constructors standing | exchange
rows.beside: Used as the context type K of Contextual (Context.lean). No dependence-name counterpart; a plainer name would be 'ChangeMeasure' or 'ChangeAccount'.
rows.docstring: Two readings of change: by standing, and by exchange.

rows.name: Flow.changeReadings
rows.states: A contextual system over steps that gives, for each condition c and step t, two pairs (rise, fall): by standing, (level(t+1) − level(t), level(t) − level(t+1)); by exchange, (given − taken, taken − given), truncated subtraction. Every condition lies within both contexts. The two pairs are equal exactly where level(t+1) + taken = level(t) + given (balance).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Flow F C and Web F C to Contextual Nat ChangeReading C (Nat × Nat) (within := always True, shows := the two computed pairs)
rows.beside: Agreement/gluing are Contextual.Agree and Contextual.Glues (Context.lean; Glues s := one context-free assignment equals every context's value). Ties: changes_agree_iff ((b−a, a−b) = (q−p, p−q) ↔ b + p = a + q), Flow.changeReadings_agree_iff, changeReadings_glue_iff, changeReadings_glue_everywhere_iff (glues at every t ↔ L.Balances W), changeReadings_free_iff, changeReadings_glue_counting_rest, World.unity.
rows.docstring: What each reading reads of the change of each condition across the step from `t`, as what it rose and what it fell: standing reads the rise and the fall of the level; exchange reads what the flow gave beyond what it took, and took beyond what it gave.

rows.name: Sound
rows.states: For a predicate B : M → W → Prop (which worlds a state admits), the configuration (w, m) satisfies B m w: the world is among those the state admits.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on W × M, parameterized by B : M → W → Prop
rows.beside: Shown closed with «闭» (GrammarLaws) under the loop relation joint: closed_of_keptBy gives «闭» (joint world sense update act) (Sound B) from KeptBy. ClosedUnder in Frame.lean is the same closure shape; no theorem in this module ties them.
rows.docstring: The configurations at which the state's reading holds of the world.

rows.name: KeptBy
rows.states: The admitted-worlds predicate B : M → W → Prop is preserved by the update under every act: if state m admits w and the world moves from w to w' under any act a, then the updated state update m a (sense w') admits w'. A closure (invariance) condition of B along world moves, with the state updated from the act and the sensed value of the new world.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (world : W → A → W → Prop, sense : W → O, update : M → A → O → M, B : M → W → Prop)
rows.beside: Closure «闭» (GrammarLaws: ∀ x y, P x → R x y → P y). Theorem closed_of_keptBy: KeptBy … B → «闭» (joint world sense update act) (Sound B) for every act policy; kept_iff_closed ties closure to preservation along every finite reach «及». keeps_iff_leadsInto, keeps_continues_iff, keeping_policy_iff use it. Trivial cases: everything_kept, nothing_kept (preservation carries no information).
rows.docstring: **A reading kept by the update**: wherever the state reads the world and the world becomes `w'` under any act, the updated state reads `w'`.

rows.name: Possible
rows.states: For a history of (act, sensed value) pairs, newest first, the set of worlds compatible with it: the empty history gives the start worlds; (a, o) :: h gives the worlds w' such that some w compatible with h moves to w' under a and sense w' = o. It is the forward image of the starts along the recorded acts, filtered by the recorded values.
rows.shape: FUNCTION List (A × O) → (W → Prop), i.e. a SET of worlds for each history, defined by recursion on the list
rows.beside: Ties: possible_kept (KeptBy world sense record (Possible …)); possible_least (it is the least predicate preserved by recording that holds at the starts); possible_of_reached / reached_of_possible (with Generated act); history_keeps_iff, history_continues_iff. Structurally an iterated image related to «依» (GrammarConditionals: every Q y has an R-predecessor in P), but no theorem ties them.
rows.docstring: **The worlds possible after a history**: where a course from a start, taking the history's acts and sensing its values, could be.

rows.name: the module as a whole: what a 'reading' is here
rows.states: A 'reading' is a predicate B : M → W → Prop assigning to each internal state the set of worlds it admits. The module's laws are about this predicate being preserved along the joint world-and-state step (KeptBy, closure «闭»), about acts that lead only into a task from every admitted world (LeadsInto, LeadsIntoEnabled), and about the compatible-world set of a recorded history (Possible). In Loop, the 'reading' is instead the list of candidate prediction functions not yet contradicted by the answers so far (Loop.keep, kept_iff). The sections on sensing (sensed_alike_iff, alike_within, observed_alike) state that two worlds give one sensed course exactly where they answer the acts alike.
rows.shape: PREDICATE B : M → W → Prop (state-indexed set of admitted worlds); Loop: a STRUCTURE whose internal part holds a List H of candidates
rows.beside: «闭» via closed_of_keptBy and kept_iff_closed; «及» (reach). The sensing-alike results connect to Blanketed.agent_through_sensory (Blanket.lean) and Untested.floor_forgoes is a case of alike_of_kept. No DependsOnlyOn/GoAlike tie stated in this module.
rows.docstring: what senses, predicts and chooses is the internal part of one determined law, told apart by which part reads which

rows.name: Flow.InheritsReading
rows.states: For a flow L on a web W and a labelling read : X -> Sig: for every step t and relata x, g, if x descends from g across the step from t (g is present at t, g gives x a positive amount, and x comes to stand across the step; Evolution's DescendsAt), then x's label equals g's label. The label is constant along every descent edge, in the direction parent g to offspring x.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (flow L, web W, labelling read : X -> Sig); body: forall t x g, L.DescendsAt W t x g -> read x = read g
rows.beside: ReadingsSpread's Flow.RevisesBy names the general relation (offspring's label = upd (parent's label) (what was sensed)); InheritsReading is RevisesBy with the identity update, by theorem Flow.inheritsReading_iff (ReadingsSpread.lean). Consequence in this module: Flow.lineOf_carries (every member of every cohort of lineOf has the founders' label). Tied by: Flow.inheritsReading_iff.
rows.docstring: Readings are inherited along descent in the flow: whoever descends from a relatum carries its reading.

rows.name: ReadingsPersist.Habitat.Reading
rows.states: A three-valued type of labels, own | source | whole, for the witness's line. The labels have no content of their own: all that distinguishes them is two functions of them, draw (units the line's slot takes from the source s per step when standing and fed: own 2, source 1, whole 1) and clears (whether the slot takes the habitat h at the first step: own true, source true, whole false), which enter the line's conduct and so act back sigma. The docstring's 'what the members count' is not modelled beyond these two numbers.
rows.shape: INDUCTIVE TYPE with three constructors (own, source, whole); used as the index Sig of act : Reading -> ExchangeLaw Rel Rel
rows.beside: none found as a separate name; its effect is carried by draw, clears and act back sigma in the same namespace. Not tied by a theorem to DependsOnlyOn or Sensitive.
rows.docstring: What the line's members count: their own line only, the line and the source it draws on, or everything, the dweller included.

rows.name: ExchangeLaw.ReadsThroughOwn
rows.states: For a label-indexed family of exchange laws act : Sig -> ExchangeLaw X X, a web W and a coupling relation obs: for every label sigma, every relatum h, every step t and any two level histories l, l', if l and l' are alike through h's couplings at every step up to t (W admits h under both or neither, and every condition c with obs h c has the same level under both), then act sigma gives h the same take and the same give toward every condition across the step from t. What h exchanges depends only on the levels coupled into h and on h's admission, for every label and every relatum.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (act : Sig -> ExchangeLaw X X, W : Web X X, obs : X -> X -> Prop); body: forall sigma h t l l', W.AlikeThroughUpTo obs h l l' t -> (act sigma).GivesAlike t h l l'
rows.beside: Counterfactual.lean's ExchangeLaw.Through W obs part names the same relation for the relata outside a part (part h = false), built from Testing's Web.AlikeThroughUpTo and Counterfactual's GivesAlike. Theorem ReadsThroughOwn.through_act gives (act sigma).Through W obs part for every sigma and every part (one direction only; the converse is not stated, though it would follow at the all-false part). Theorem byReading_through gives (byReading act read).Through W obs part.
rows.docstring: Each relatum's act, whatever reading it carries, reads only what couples into that relatum.

rows.name: RemovesItsReaders
rows.states: For a selection select on courses, an assignment slotsOf of slots to line indices, a set of line indices readers, and a course l: the course l satisfies select, and some line i in the set readers is removed by l (RemovesLine: some slot of i has positive level at step 0, and there is a step T from which no slot of i has positive level). The set readers is a free argument; the definition does not relate it to what select depends on, or to anything else about select.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (select : (Nat -> X -> Nat) -> Prop, slotsOf : I -> X -> Prop, readers : I -> Prop, l : Nat -> X -> Nat); body: select l AND exists i, readers i AND RemovesLine slotsOf l i
rows.beside: RemovesLine (same module) is its second conjunct, with RemovesLine.not_standsLate (a removed line does not stand late). Witness: Habitat.cleared_removes_its_readers, with readers := (i = .d), the dweller's line, whose slots are fed only while the habitat stands (fed: d0, d1 need level of h at least 1). No name without the word for the whole conjunction.
rows.docstring: the selection holds at a course that removes a line of readers from the pool that course gives.

rows.name: ExchangeLaw.byReading
rows.states: Given a label-indexed family of exchange laws act : Sig -> ExchangeLaw X X and a labelling read : X -> Sig, the exchange law in which each relatum h, at every step, under every history, toward every condition, takes and gives exactly what act (read h) gives h. A composition: the relatum's label picks which law governs that relatum's exchanges.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (act : Sig -> ExchangeLaw X X, read : X -> Sig) to ExchangeLaw X X; body: take t h l c = (act (read h)).take t h l c, give likewise
rows.beside: Counterfactual's ExchangeLaw.withAct part act' (a part acting by one law, the rest by another). Theorem byReading_withAct: where every member of part has label sig, byReading act read agrees on take and give with (byReading act read).withAct part (act sig). Also byReading_nonanticipating, byReading_through, and the witnesses Habitat.world_byReading and ReadingsSpread.Commons.world_byReading.
rows.docstring: Every relatum carries a reading (`read`), and across each step exchanges as the act that reading gives (`act`, Bound's act indexed by what is carried).

rows.name: ReadingsPersist.Habitat.readOf
rows.states: For a label sigma, the labelling of the witness's relata that gives sigma to the line's two slots a0, a1 (isA x = true) and the label whole to every other relatum (s, h, d0, d1), whose conduct does not use the label.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Reading x Rel to Reading; body: bif isA x then sigma else .whole
rows.beside: isA (the line's slots). Theorem Habitat.world_byReading: byReading (act back) (readOf sigma) has the same take and give as world back sigma = (restLaw back).withAct isA (act back sigma). Theorem Habitat.inherits: (flowOf back sigma lev).InheritsReading (webOf lev) (readOf sigma); Habitat.lineA_carries.
rows.docstring: The readings carried when the line carries `σ`: the line `σ`, every other relatum everything (the others' conduct does not depend on it).

rows.name: ReadingsSpread.Commons.Reading
rows.states: A three-valued type of labels, own | source | whole, for the commons witness's focal line. As in ReadingsPersist, the labels differ only through two functions: drawS (units a focal slot takes from the source per step when standing and fed: own 2, source 1, whole 2, so here whole draws two, unlike ReadingsPersist's draw where whole draws one) and clears (own true, source true, whole false: whether the focal slot takes one unit of the habitat while it stands, and then also passes its standing to a second slot n0->n1, n2->n3).
rows.shape: INDUCTIVE TYPE with three constructors (own, source, whole); the index of act back : Reading -> ExchangeLaw Rel Rel
rows.beside: none found as a separate name; its effect is carried by drawS, clears and act in the same namespace. A distinct type from ReadingsPersist.Habitat.Reading with the same constructor names; no theorem ties the two.
rows.docstring: The focal line's reading: its own line only, the line and its source, or everything.

rows.name: read (ReadingsSpread.Revised.read, ReadingsSpread.Contact.read; and the parameter read : α -> Sig)
rows.states: Two witness tables and one generic parameter. Revised.read : Nat -> Bool gives true to members 0, 2, 3, 4 and false to 1 and every member from 5 on: which members of Revised.generations carry the label true (the docstring's 'narrow'). Contact.read : Nat -> Bool gives false to member 1 and true to every other. In the module's general part, read : α -> Sig is a variable naming any assignment of a label to each member, used by Generations.RevisesBy (kid's label = upd (parent's label) (what the parent sensed)), ClosedFrom, carrying (amount 1 where inR of the label holds, else 0), revisedIn/revisedOut (counts of parent-kid pairs where the label crosses into / out of the region inR), and standingCount.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from member index (Nat) to Bool (the two witnesses); in general a FUNCTION from members α to labels Sig (a parameter, not a definition)
rows.beside: No name without the word for the labelling itself; the relations over it are named Generations.RevisesBy, ClosedFrom, carrying, revisedIn, revisedOut. Ties for the witnesses: Revised.rises_then_revised (counts under carrying read id); Contact.removed_revises (removed.RevisesBy read (fun t p => read (senseSelf t p)) copy, so each kid's label equals its parent's) and Contact.removed_locked (every member from step 1 on has label true, via fixed_of_present).
rows.docstring: Member `0` carries the narrow reading, `1` the wide one; later members carry the narrow one.

rows.name: ReadingsSpread.Contact.readMet
rows.states: A table Nat -> Bool giving true to members 0 and 2 and false to every other: the labels in the course met (cohort 0 = [0, 1]; 0's kid is 3, 1's kid is 4). With senseOther pairing member 0 with member 1 (and every other member with itself) and update copy, each kid's label equals the label of the member its parent is paired with, so 3, the kid of 0, takes 1's label false.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from member index (Nat) to Bool
rows.beside: Generations.RevisesBy in the same module. Theorems: met_revises (met.RevisesBy readMet (fun t p => readMet (senseOther t p)) copy) and met_replaced (3 is in cohort 1 and readMet 3 is not true, via Generations.revised_out).
rows.docstring: Members `3` on carry the wide reading in this course.

rows.name: ReadingsSpread.Commons.readOf
rows.states: For a label sigma, the labelling of the commons witness's relata that gives sigma to the focal line's four slots n0, n1, n2, n3 (isFocal x = true) and the label whole to every other relatum (w0, w1, s, h, d0, d1), whose conduct does not use the label.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from Reading x Rel to Reading; body: bif isFocal x then sigma else .whole
rows.beside: isFocal (the focal slots). Theorem Commons.world_byReading: byReading (act back) (readOf sigma) has the same take and give as world back sigma = (restLaw back).withAct isFocal (act back sigma).
rows.docstring: The readings carried when the focal line carries `σ`: every other relatum reads everything.

rows.name: ReadsNoOrder
rows.states: For a statement `law` taking a datum d and an order `better` on configurations: for every datum d and every two orders, if law holds at d with the first order it holds at d with the second. So the truth of law at each datum is the same under every order; the order makes no difference to it.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on a statement law : D → (S → S → Prop) → Prop (def ReadsNoOrder {D} (law) : Prop := ∀ d better better', law d better → law d better').
rows.beside: No name without "read" found for this relation in the module or its imports. Its docstring says it is the pattern of Significance.ReadsOnlyDynamics (also a read-name), with the order in place of the significance. The theorem ReadsNoOrder.not_entails uses it: such a statement, if it entails C (Comparison) at d on a frame with an Extension, fails at d for every order. PremisesTogether.ListedPaths.condition_reads_no_order gives an instance.
rows.docstring: A statement about some data and an order on configurations reads no order when its truth does not change with the order

rows.name: reading (IdleStep.reading)
rows.states: A function on step numbers that sends 0 to 0 and n+1 to n. Steps 0 and 1 both go to 0 (step 0 is idle), and after that each step goes one further (each later step moves). It is the witness stuttering: it sends each step of the world to a step of the course with the idle steps removed.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat → Nat (a concrete definition in namespace IdleStep).
rows.beside: Stutter (Stuttering.lean) is the relation's name without "read": ρ 0 = 0, each step stays or goes up by one, and every step is hit.
