Stutter.Moves (IdleRemoval.lean) relates it to `moving` (s ↦ s+1), and World.IdleAt (IdleRemoval.lean) says nothing takes part and every relatum is unmoved at its idle steps. Tied by IdleStep.stutter : Stutter reading, IdleStep.moves : Stutter.Moves reading moving, IdleStep.idle : world.IdleAt reading, and IdleStep.premises_hold. A second, unrelated docstring use in the same module is MatchedCourses.lossesAlike ("The reading relating the non-base claims and the base only to itself"): an equivalence relation on Claim, with no read-name.
rows.docstring: The reading idle at the first step and moving at every other.

rows.name: field read (Presentation.read)
rows.states: The second field of a Presentation (the first is encode : M → C). It is a relation between codes and questions: read c q is the proposition that code c answers yes to question q. Exact answers p says that for every configuration m and question q, read (encode m) q ↔ answers m q, so the code-side relation reproduces the configuration's answers.
rows.shape: STRUCTURE FIELD of type C → Q → Prop (a binary relation from codes to questions) in structure Presentation M Q C.
rows.beside: The configuration-side counterpart is `answers : M → Q → Prop`, the family fixed before any code. They are tied by the definition Exact (∀ m q, p.read (p.encode m) q ↔ answers m q). canonical_exact proves the canonical presentation (encode := answers, read := fun c q => c q) exact, and matches_iff_equal_answers relates two presentations' codes by ∀ q, p.read c q ↔ r.read d q. The field itself has no non-read name.
rows.docstring: A code for each configuration and a reading of each code at each question.

rows.name: Formula.read
rows.states: Given a formula φ whose atoms are `none` and `some y`, the fixed propositions `fixed`, and a proposition a: the proposition φ states when atom none stands for a and atom some y stands for fixed y. In other words, a is put into φ's one open slot with the other atoms held fixed. The result is φ.eval (Formula.atoms fixed a).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (φ : Formula (Option β)), (fixed : β → Prop) and (a : Prop) to Prop; for fixed φ and fixed it is a function Prop → Prop.
rows.beside: Formula.eval is the same relation without "read": by definition Formula.read φ fixed a = φ.eval (Formula.atoms fixed a). Formula.read_congr (from Formula.eval_congr) says that interderivable a ↔ b give interderivable φ.read fixed a ↔ φ.read fixed b, with no axiom. In the module's terms (Learning.Lumped relation), lumped_iff and extensional_iff_lumped say the stronger demand, that every function Prop → V take one value at both ends of every interderivation, is propext; byName (fun p => p) is the case that needs it.
rows.docstring: The reading of a proposition through a formula, the other atoms held fixed.

rows.name: ReadsOnlyActsAlong
rows.states: For a Turns system T, a position k and a world w: for every member n ≥ k and every two couplings o, o', T.law n o (T.acts w n) = T.law n o' (T.acts w n). So at the list of earlier acts that world w actually produces, the act of each member from k on is the same whatever its own coupling. Member n's coupling makes no difference to its act at that history, though it may at other lists of acts.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (k : Nat) and (w : W), given T : Turns W O A.
rows.beside: LawAlikeAlong k w w' (same module) is the weaker, two-world form: the act is the same for the couplings of w and of w' at w's history. lawAlikeAlong_of_along derives it for every w' from ReadsOnlyActsAlong. The every-list form is Cascade's ReadsOnlyActsFrom (also a read-name), and readsOnlyActsAlong_of_from goes from it to this one. The consequence is stated with a non-read name: cascade_through_along gives Learning.Training.Through (T.AlikeBefore k) for any selection on acts, where AlikeBefore k w w' says the couplings of members before k are equal. Turns.Unreached.along and not_from show the predicate is strictly weaker than ReadsOnlyActsFrom.
rows.docstring: From member `k` on, every member acts alike whatever its own coupling at the list of acts world `w` gives it: at the histories `w` reaches, not on every list.

rows.name: readFrom (Window.readFrom)
rows.states: A function from a bound N and a step t to the state at step t of one fixed witness course, lossCourse 1 0 3 5 2 0 N with the rule recomputed at every step from the start `even`. The state is ((counts of carriers and others, loss counter), rule in force). The loss counter starts at 0 and grows by one a step. In the pooled rule the others' return is lo = 2 while the counter is below N and lo' = 0 once it reaches N; the shapers' return is hi = 5 throughout. N is the step from which the others' return switches.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat → Nat → (CarrierCounts × Nat) × CarrierCounts (an abbrev of the bound and the step).
rows.beside: lossCourse (same module) is the general form, and readFrom N t unfolds to it by definition (abbrev); lossCourse in turn abbreviates course / Thinned.course over shapedLossPool (Thinned.lossPool), whose switch is Nat.ble (ℓ+1) N. The theorems on readFrom are Window.in_time (switching at N = 2: Locked the other way from step 4), Window.between and Window.too_late (switching at N = 3: not turned, locked in the shapers' favour from step 6). No name without "read" for the switch itself.
rows.docstring: The course in which the others read the loss from step `N`.

rows.name: ReadableInTime (Web.ReadableInTime)
rows.states: For a web W, a group of formations, the feasible courses, a property keeps of courses, and two courses l (the losing one) and l': there is a step T such that T is the first step apart of l and l' for the group (FirstApart: some member's admission differs between l and l' at T, and every member's admission agrees at every earlier step) and l is still Recoverable at T (some feasible course agreeing with l at every step up to T has keeps).
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (W, group, feasible, keeps, l, l'): ∃ T, W.FirstApart group l l' T ∧ Recoverable feasible keeps l T.
rows.beside: Built from FirstApart and Recoverable / NoReturnAt (same module), which are its non-read parts. readableInTime_iff: given FirstApart at T and NoReturnAt at N, it holds exactly where T < N. Failures are given by too_late_of_alike, too_late_of_unreached, too_late_within_margin and too_late_of_own. Admission alike up to a step is tied to SelectsThroughAll thresholdOnly / AlikeThroughAll by alikeThroughAll_thresholdOnly_iff.
rows.docstring: Readable in time: the first step at which a selection read off the group's continuations can tell the losing course `l` from `l'` is a step at which `l` is still recoverable.

rows.name: ReadsInTime (Web.ReadsInTime)
rows.states: For a family of selections sel (one predicate on courses for each step), feasible, keeps and two courses l and l': there is a step T at which the family first separates l and l' (TellsApartAt: sel T gives them different truth values, and every sel s with s < T gives them the same), and l is still Recoverable at T.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (sel : Nat → (Nat → C → Nat) → Prop, feasible, keeps, l, l'): ∃ T, TellsApartAt sel l l' T ∧ Recoverable feasible keeps l T.
rows.beside: Built from TellsApartAt and Recoverable (same module, no read-names). ReadsInTime.readable: if each sel s is a selection through the group's couplings up to s by threshold only (Selection.SelectsThroughAll thresholdOnly group s (sel s), i.e. histories AlikeThroughAll are selected alike) and FirstApart holds at T, then ReadsInTime gives ReadableInTime. This rests on TellsApartAt.not_before (the family separates no earlier than the first step apart).
rows.docstring: A family of selections reads in time: it tells the losing course `l` from `l'` apart at a step at which `l` is still recoverable.

rows.name: near, mid (FourReaders.Formation.near / .mid: the two gauges)
rows.states: Two constructors of the witness's Formation type. A gauge is a formation that takes and gives nothing (take and give are 0 for it) and whose only requirement is the habitat. Its need is 3 for near and 2 for mid. So its admission at a step is exactly 'the habitat level at that step is at least its need'. Under the never-stop course the habitat goes 4,3,2,1,0, and under the spared course s0 it stays 4. So near's admission first differs between the two courses at step 2 and mid's at step 3; the cleared course's point of no return is step 3.
rows.shape: CONSTRUCTORS of the inductive Formation (elements of a finite type), given their meaning by the clauses of flow, requires and need.
rows.beside: Their relation to the habitat is stated without "read" by requires/need and Web.Admits (Admission.lean: every required condition's level is at least the need), and by only_habitat_near and only_habitat_mid (a gauge requires only the habitat). The theorems near_firstApart (FirstApart at 2) and mid_firstApart (at 3) tie them to FirstApart. near_inTime gives ReadableInTime via readableInTime_iff and noReturn, with its gap against its margin 4 − 3; mid_atThePoint gives not ReadableInTime while the dweller is still admitted at step 3. The word 'gauge' appears only in docstrings and has no definition of its own.
rows.docstring: Needs: the near gauge 3, the mid gauge 2, the first relay 4, every other need 1.

rows.name: ExchangeLaw.ReadsInto
rows.states: For every formation h with part h = false, every step t, condition c and histories l, l' : Nat -> C -> Nat: if l and l' agree at every (s, d) with s <= t and reads t h c s d = true, then law.take t h l c = law.take t h l' c and law.give t h l c = law.give t h l' c. So what h takes from and gives to c across the step from t is the same under any two histories that agree on the levels the schedule marks for (t, h, c).
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (law : ExchangeLaw F C, part : F -> Bool, reads : Nat -> F -> C -> Nat -> C -> Bool); a per-condition dependence-only-on statement
rows.beside: Thresholds.ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt is the same relation per formation (gives alike, one schedule for all conditions); tied by ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt.readsInto (ReadsAt -> ReadsInto) and ExchangeLaw.Through.readsInto (Counterfactual's Through -> ReadsInto). Propagation's ExchangeLaw.RespondsWithin (coupling strength) is tied by ExchangeLaw.ReadsInto.respondsWithin_unread: an unmarked level has RespondsWithin strength 0; ExchangeLaw.ReadsInto.restrict: the strengths restricted to marked levels (restrictInto) are RespondsWithin strengths. Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn has the same general shape for a Process; no theorem ties it to ReadsInto.
rows.docstring: **The law reads into each condition a schedule.** Across the step from `t`, what each formation

rows.name: readCouplings
rows.states: Turns a schedule into strengths: the strength at (t, h, c, s, d) is 1 where reads t h c s d = true and 0 elsewhere (the indicator of the schedule). It is restrictInto reads with every strength set to 1.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from a schedule (Nat -> F -> C -> Nat -> C -> Bool) to strengths (Nat -> F -> C -> Nat -> C -> Nat)
rows.beside: Its routes are Couples/CouplesAt/Upstream (Loops, Remainder) taken at these strengths. couplesAt_readCouplings: CouplesAt at restrictInto reads k implies CouplesAt at readCouplings reads; upstream_readCouplings: the same for Upstream under strengthsBefore T. apart_only_downstream and exchange_alike_off_downstream state their conclusions with Upstream over strengthsBefore t (readCouplings reads).
rows.docstring: The routes of reading: one where the schedule marks a level read into a condition, zero

rows.name: Observation.Measure.reads
rows.states: The witness schedule for Measure.law T N (one formation, two conditions: stock = true, record = false): reads T t () c s d is true exactly when s = t and either c is the stock and d is the record, or c is the record, d is the stock and T <= t. So the draw from the stock depends on the record at the same step, and what is added to the record depends, from step T on, on the stock at the same step.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from T : Nat to a schedule Nat -> Unit -> Bool -> Nat -> Bool -> Bool
rows.beside: Tied to ExchangeLaw.ReadsInto by Observation.Measure.readsInto: (law T N).ReadsInto (fun _ => false) (reads T). No separate name without read.
rows.docstring: What it reads: into the stock, the record at the step; into the record, from `T` on, the stock

rows.name: readAt
rows.states: Given a quantity q : Passage -> Nat and a list of passages Q, sends a position some j to q (pick Q j), the quantity of the passage at position j of Q, and no position (none) to 0. It is an evaluation at a position, not a dependence relation.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (q : Passage -> Nat) (Q : List Passage) : Option Nat -> Nat
rows.beside: Siblings of the same shape without read: beforeAt, afterAt, cellAt. Theorems taken_node and given_node: the witness flow's taken/given at node x equals readAt Passage.taken (P t) (track σ ρ x t) / readAt Passage.given ...; cellAt_total: the column total of cellAt equals readAt q Q; readAt_pos: a positive value comes from some position j with 0 < q (pick Q j). Not about dependence-only-on.
rows.docstring: A reading of the passage at a position, nothing at no position.

rows.name: World.ReadOffExchange
rows.states: A world w is ReadOffExchange when there exist an exchange relation rel over w's relata and a list of present relata at each step such that w's flow is a run of rel along w's levels (at each t the flow's present list is present t and its take/give are admitted by rel under those levels), and every requirement w.web.requires t f c is matched by rel.RespondsBelow at the need: under every history differing from the actual at most in c's level at t, with that level below w.web.need t f c, no exchange admitted by rel has f exchanging. So the world's flow is generated by some exchange relation, and each requirement is a necessary stop of the requiring relatum's exchange when the required level falls below the need.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on a World (an existential over an ExchangeRelation and a presence schedule)
rows.beside: No name without read for the same relation. Tied by ExchangeRelation.Runs.readOffExchange (every run of a relation, with any need, gives such a world), ExchangeLaw.readWorld_readOffExchange (every law's course does), World.ReadOffExchange.dependent (implies w.withRest.Dependent; one direction only), World.takingUnsupported_not_readOff (not every world is one).
rows.docstring: **The world is read off a relation of exchange**: its flow is a run, along its standings, of a

rows.name: NotReadmitted
rows.states: For every configuration p and rule g, if present p is false then present (f p g) is false: the set of configurations where present fails is closed under the step f, for every rule.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (present : A × B -> Prop, f : A × B -> R -> A × B)
rows.beside: Same shape as Frame.ClosedUnder (the grammar's «闭») with rel p q := exists g, q = f p g and region := not present, and as Frame.Invariant for not present; no theorem in this module ties them. Used in closed_stays_closed; instance stands_not_readmitted: NotReadmitted (Stands K) (join fA fB) where the loss accrues.
rows.docstring: **The selection brings no reader of the beyond back** once none is in the pool.

rows.name: ReadsThroughPresent
rows.states: For every configuration p and rule g, if present p is false then h p g = hA p.1 g: wherever present fails, the next rule given by h equals hA applied to the share component p.1 alone, so h there does not vary with the second component.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (present : A × B -> Prop, hA : A -> R -> R, h : A × B -> R -> R)
rows.beside: With present everywhere false it says h = ClosedCapture.joinRead hA; ClosedCapture.Unread states h independent of the second component everywhere (no theorem ties ReadsThroughPresent to Unread). read_absent: two configurations where present fails and with equal share give the same h. window_through: ReadsThroughPresent (Stands K) hA (windowRead hA hL N K); window_unread: with K <= N, ReadsThroughPresent (fun _ => False) hA (windowRead ...).
rows.docstring: **Where no reader of what lies beyond the share is in the pool, the rule read is the

rows.name: boundRead
rows.states: boundRead hA hL p g = windowRead hA hL 0 p.2.2 (p.1, p.2.1) g: on a configuration (share, loss, bound), the next rule is hL (share, loss) g when loss < bound and hA share g otherwise; the window with lower end 0 and upper end taken from the configuration's third coordinate.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (hA : A -> R -> R) (hL : A × Nat -> R -> R) : A × Nat × Nat -> R -> R
rows.beside: bound_course: the paced course of withBound fA fB with boundRead hA hL equals the window's course with K fixed, K carried as a coordinate. boundRead_reads: RuleCapture.ReadsShare (boundOrder P) M (boundRead hA hL), i.e. boundRead is monotone in share, in loss and, reversed, in the bound (given monoL and against). ReadsShare is itself monotonicity: P.le x y -> M.le (h x g) (h y g').
rows.docstring: The window read with its bound taken from the configuration, the readers reading from when they

rows.name: readLoss
rows.states: A witness: the constant function sending every (counts, loss) and rule to lo. Used as hL in window := windowRead (threshold hi lo) readLoss 0 4.
rows.shape: FUNCTION CarrierCounts × Nat -> CarrierCounts -> CarrierCounts (constant lo)
rows.beside: No relation named; it is the hL argument of windowRead in the Drained witness (Drained.premises, clock_turned, strong_undone, weak_turned).
rows.docstring: The readers of the loss read the rule as `lo` from when they stand.

rows.name: windowRead
rows.states: windowRead hA hL N K p g is hL p g when N <= p.2 < K and hA p.1 g otherwise: while the loss coordinate lies in [N, K) the next rule is given by hL from the whole configuration, and outside it by hA from the share alone.
rows.shape: FUNCTION (hA : A -> R -> R) (hL : A × Nat -> R -> R) (N K : Nat) : A × Nat -> R -> R
rows.beside: Stands K p := p.2 < K. window_through: ReadsThroughPresent (Stands K) hA (windowRead hA hL N K); window_unread: K <= N gives ReadsThroughPresent (fun _ => False), i.e. windowRead equals hA on the share everywhere; window_past: for K <= p.2, windowRead hA hL N K p g = ClosedCapture.joinRead hA p g.
rows.docstring: **The readers of the loss read it as `hL` while it lies in `[N, K)`**; elsewhere the rule is read

rows.name: physicalReads
rows.states: In the witness situation s, sends each domain d to none when the actual model's vulnerability of d fails under s.roots, and otherwise to some (observed s.installation []), the installation's epoch, serial, address [] and the key located at it. It is a report of the installation's state by the members that still work.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Situation -> Readings, where Readings := Domain -> Option Observation (abbrev in Transactions.lean)
rows.beside: Sibling without read: physicalApprovals (Situation -> Approvals, Domain -> Option Request). Used by respond (guardedExecute ... (physicalReads s) (physicalApprovals s)). Transactions.observed gives the reported value. Not a dependence-only-on relation.
rows.docstring: Members the actual faults leave working report the installation; failed ones withhold.

rows.name: readResponses, readFaithful (hypotheses of member_completes and pooled_completes); reads : Readings
rows.states: Not definitions: hypothesis names. readResponses: every roster member d not failed under roots has reads d = some (expected p) (it reports what the request expects). readFaithful: for such d, any reported o with reads d = some o equals observed w p.address (the report matches the installation at the request's address). reads is a variable of type Readings := Domain -> Option Observation.
rows.shape: hypotheses (propositions over d) in theorems; reads a FUNCTION Domain -> Option Observation
rows.beside: Paired with issueResponses / issueFaithful on approvals, same shape without read; passed to Transactions.certified_completes, whose own hypotheses carry the same names.
rows.docstring: none (hypothesis names)

rows.name: poolReady, every_candidate_ready_pool_not
rows.states: False matches: the letters 'read' inside 'ready'. poolReady is readiness of a fault envelope on four members; nothing about dependence.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Envelope -> Bool; a theorem
rows.beside: none found (not about this)
rows.docstring: Readiness of a listed envelope on the four members.

rows.name: ReadsShare
rows.states: The rule function h : S → R → R is order-preserving in the share alone. For any shares x, y with P.le x y, and any two prior rules g, g' (taken independently), M.le (h x g) (h y g'). So a share no lower gives a resulting rule no lower, whatever rule each was applied to. The second argument makes no difference to the order, so h's output order depends only on the share.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (P : Preorder S, M : Preorder R, h : S → R → R)
rows.beside: Ideals.Monotone P Q f (Ideals.lean:630, ∀ a b, P.le a b → Q.le (f a) (f b)) is the same relation for a one-argument map. ReadsShare is that monotonicity holding uniformly across the ignored second argument (even across different g, g'). No theorem ties ReadsShare to Ideals.Monotone. Theorems on it: ReadsShare.reverse (reversing both orders keeps it), ReadsShare.pair (closed under pairing), and proportional_reads, threshold, byMargin (instances).
rows.docstring: **The rule read is a monotone function of the share alone.** The rule read at a share not lower is not lower, whatever rules the two readings meet.

rows.name: pairReading
rows.states: The componentwise product of two rule-update functions. From h₁ : S → R₁ → R₁ and h₂ : S → R₂ → R₂ it builds the function taking a share x and a pair of rules (g₁, g₂) to (h₁ x g₁, h₂ x g₂). The same share feeds both components.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (S → R₁ → R₁) × (S → R₂ → R₂) to (S → R₁ × R₂ → R₁ × R₂)
rows.beside: No name without 'read' (it is Prod.map of h₁ x and h₂ x at a shared x). Tie: ReadsShare.pair says that if h₁ and h₂ are each monotone in the share, then pairReading h₁ h₂ is monotone in the share under pairOrder M₁ M₂. pair_locks uses it.
rows.docstring: Two rules, each read from the share.

rows.name: readAll
rows.states: Not a dependence relation. It is a list operation: it applies a partial decoding function res : List α → Option M to each group in a list of groups. It returns some of the list of results when every group decodes, and none if any group fails (the Option traverse/mapM).
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (List α → Option M) and List (List α) to Option (List M)
rows.beside: Equivalent to List.mapM res in Option, but no such name is used. Tie: readAll_map_iff says readAll res (ws.map word) = some (ws.map meaning) exactly when res (word w) = some (meaning w) for each w in ws. reads_every_iff lifts this through chunks/encode. SharedCodes.lean uses it at lines 785 and 809.
rows.docstring: Read each group; `none` where some group is not read.

rows.name: ReadsCouplings
rows.states: A widened level-coupling relation built from obs, o and a. Formation g is coupled by level to condition c when obs g c holds, or when g is o and c is coupled into a: W.CoupledInto obs a c, meaning a depends on c by threshold (W.DependsOn) or obs a c. So o gets, in addition to its own level couplings, a level coupling to everything coupled into a.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (W : Web F C, obs : F → C → Prop, o a : F) to a relation F → C → Prop (a coupling-by-level relation)
rows.beside: It is an instance of a coupling-by-level relation 'obs', fed to Web.AlikeThrough, SelectsThrough and CoupledInto (Testing.lean). Ties: AlikeThrough.of_reads says that two histories alike through o under ReadsCouplings are alike through o under obs and through a under obs. SelectsThroughAll.reads says that a selection through the pooled coupling of o and a is a selection through o under ReadsCouplings. Flow.withinCoupling_reads and withinCoupling_reads_iff say that o's coupling closure lies within, or equals, the union of o's and a's closures.
rows.docstring: `o` reads `a`'s couplings: beside the coupling by level `obs`, `o` is coupled by level into every condition coupled into `a`, by threshold or by level.

rows.name: ReadsWithin
rows.states: At step t, for formation h, under history l, the law's exchange depends only on the conditions in the list cs. Take any history l' that has the same levels as l on every condition in cs at every step s ≤ t. Then the law gives h the same take and give at t under l and l' (law.GivesAlike t h l l'). The relation is anchored at l, and the agreement is required only on cs, up to t.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (law : ExchangeLaw F C, t : Nat, h : F, l : Nat → C → Nat, cs : List C)
rows.beside: A restricted form of ExchangeLaw.Nonanticipating (Counterfactual.lean: the exchange at t depends only on levels up to t, on all conditions) and of InsensitiveAt (agreement on all but one condition). Ties: Nonanticipating.readsWithin_of_every says that when cs lists every condition, Nonanticipating gives ReadsWithin. alike_of_sensitive_agree_within says that under Nonanticipating and ReadsWithin, agreement up to t on the conditions h is Sensitive to gives GivesAlike. No name for exactly this.
rows.docstring: At `t`, for `h`, under `l`, the law reads within the conditions of `cs`: every history agreeing with `l` on them up to `t` gives alike with `l`.

rows.name: ReadsFinitely
rows.states: For every step t, formation h and history l, there is a finite list of conditions cs such that ReadsWithin t h l cs holds. That is, the exchange at t depends only on the levels of finitely many conditions up to t, and the list may vary with t, h and l.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on law : ExchangeLaw F C
rows.beside: Ties to Nonanticipating, Sensitive and Through (Counterfactual.lean). ReadsFinitely.nonanticipating says ReadsFinitely implies Nonanticipating. Nonanticipating.readsFinitely_of_every gives the converse when the conditions are finite. ReadsFinitely.through_sensitive says it gives law.Through W law.Sensitive part. ReadsFinitely.least_coupling says Sensitive is the least coupling the law goes through, up to ¬¬. ReadsFinitely.alike_of_insensitive. Counterexamples: tailLaw_not_readsFinitely and no_list (no single list works for all t, l).
rows.docstring: The law reads finitely many conditions: at every step, for every formation and under every history, it reads within some list of conditions, the list possibly depending on the history.

rows.name: ReadsAs
rows.states: Form x is the form that code c assigns to sense n: c n = x. It is just equality of c's value at n with x, the preimage relation of the code.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (c : M → F, x : F, n : M), defined as c n = x
rows.beside: Its universal form is TellsApart (injectivity of the code, ∀ n n', c n = c n' → n = n'). Tie: self_reads_iff says that (∀ m n, c n = c m ↔ n = m) holds exactly when TellsApart c. reads_iff says that for an injective cg, the n with cg n = cf m is exactly m iff cf m = cg m. reads_other.
rows.docstring: A formation with code `c` reads the form `x` as the sense `n` where `c` gives `n` the form `x`.

rows.name: ReadsOnlyDynamics
rows.states: The statement law : D → (Pos → Nat → F → Prop) → Prop is invariant in its second argument. If it holds of dynamics d with significance sig, it holds of d with every other significance sig'. So its truth depends on d alone.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on law : D → (Pos → Nat → F → Prop) → Prop
rows.beside: none found with a non-'read' name (it is invariance, or independence, of the second argument). Ties: readsOnlyDynamics_of says any statement that factors through d alone has it. ReadsOnlyDynamics.admits_rival says such a statement holding with some sig also holds with a bounded (rival) significance. ReadsOnlyDynamics.not_entails says such a statement cannot entail Unrestricted. SignificanceStatements.lean cites it.
rows.docstring: A statement about a dynamics (a world, a web, a flow or any other) and a significance reads only the dynamics when its truth does not change with the significance.

rows.name: ReadsAt
rows.states: Given a schedule reads : Nat → F → C → Bool, the law's exchange for each formation h outside the part, across the step from t, depends only on the conditions the schedule marks true at (t, h). Take any two histories l, l' that agree, at every step s ≤ t, on every condition d with reads t h d = true. Then law.GivesAlike t h l l'.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (law : ExchangeLaw F C, part : F → Bool, reads : Nat → F → C → Bool)
rows.beside: A schedule-indexed form of ExchangeLaw.Through and Nonanticipating (Counterfactual.lean). Ties: Nonanticipating.readsAt_all says Nonanticipating gives ReadsAt with the all-true schedule. ExchangeLaw.Through.readsAt says Through gives ReadsAt for any schedule covering CoupledInto. ReadsAt.respondsWithin_unread says an unmarked condition has response strength 0. ReadsAt.restrict. ReadsBelow.standing_readsAt.
rows.docstring: **The law reads a schedule.** Across the step from `t`, for each formation `h` outside the part, the law reads only the conditions `reads t h` marks: under histories agreeing on those up to `t`, it gives alike.

rows.name: ReadsBelow
rows.states: For each formation h outside the part, across the step from t, take two histories l, l' in which stock c stands at least θ s at every step s ≤ t in both, and every condition other than c agrees at every s ≤ t. Then the law gives h alike. While c is at or above its threshold, the exchange does not depend on c's exact level, only on its being at or above θ.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (law : ExchangeLaw F C, part : F → Bool, c : C, θ : Nat → Nat)
rows.beside: Close to ExchangeLaw.InsensitiveAt (Counterfactual.lean), which drops c entirely. ReadsBelow drops c only on the region where c ≥ θ. No theorem ties it to InsensitiveAt. Ties: ExchangeLaw.Through.readsBelow says Through, with c not level-coupled and θ at least the needs, gives ReadsBelow. ReadsBelow.standing_readsAt says the standing law satisfies ReadsAt with the schedule offStock mark. ReadsBelow.standing_unread and standing_no_loop. break_carried_nowhere.
rows.docstring: **The law reads a stock only below a threshold.** For each formation outside the part, across the step from `t`: under histories alike up to `t` off the stock `c`, in both of which `c` has stood at each step `s` at least `θ s`, the law gives alike.

rows.name: restrictReads
rows.states: The strength function k with every entry for an unmarked condition set to zero. At (t, h, c, s, d), the strength is k t h c s d if the schedule marks d for h at t (reads t h d = true), and 0 otherwise.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (reads : Nat → F → C → Bool, k : Nat → F → C → Nat → C → Nat) to Nat → F → C → Nat → C → Nat (a strength function)
rows.beside: Feeds Loops.Couples, CouplesAt, Upstream and OnLoop (strength-based coupling, Loops.lean). Ties: ExchangeLaw.ReadsAt.restrict says that under ReadsAt, the restricted strengths are still response strengths of the law (RespondsWithin). couples_reads says every Couples of the restricted strengths has some formation outside the part marking d. upstream_unread and not_onLoop_unread say a condition no one marks has nothing downstream but itself and lies on no loop.
rows.docstring: The strengths restricted to what is read: a strength from a level `h` does not read at `t` is zero.

rows.name: Delayed.readAt
rows.states: For a step t and a level history l over the single condition (), the Boolean that is true exactly when the level of () at step t under l is above zero: decide (0 < l t ()). It is a function of the history alone; which formation's couplings it depends through is stated only by the theorem read_through.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat -> (Nat -> Unit -> Nat) -> Bool (a step and a level history to a Boolean)
rows.beside: In the module the generic hypothesis `read : (Nat -> C -> Nat) -> A` with `through : forall l l', W.AlikeThroughUpTo obs g l l' D -> read l = read l'` (in answer_alike_before, different_answers_not_unreached, different_answers_reached) is the dependence relation: a function of histories constant on histories alike through g's couplings up to D. Theorem Delayed.read_through ties readAt t to it: readAt t takes one value on any two histories that are AlikeThroughUpTo through formation `false` up to t. Web.ScoresThrough (Selection.lean) has the same shape for Nat-valued scores; no theorem in this module ties readAt to ScoresThrough. Delayed.answers_before_and_after: readAt 1 agrees on the two webs, readAt 2 differs.
rows.docstring: none on readAt itself; the namespace comment: "A delayed native exchange. The source is true, the distinct reader is false."

rows.name: Tower.reads
rows.states: For a tower T, reads n s is the step of level n that corresponds to step s of level 0: reads 0 s = s and reads (n+1) s = T.refine n (reads n s), i.e. the composite of the strictly increasing time maps refine (n-1) after ... after refine 0. It is a time map between levels; no knower is involved.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat -> Nat -> Nat (a level n and a level-0 step to a level-n step); defined by recursion on n inside namespace Tower with T explicit
rows.beside: No read-free name for the composite in the module; it is the time map used by Web.sample (Becoming.Sampling). Theorems: Tower.web_zero (T.web 0 = (T.web n).sample (T.reads n)), Tower.level_zero ((T.web 0).level s c = (T.web n).level (T.reads n s) c), Tower.reads_strict (Strict (T.reads n)).
rows.docstring: "The step of level `n` at which step `s` of level `0` is read."

rows.name: Training.Reads
rows.states: Given candidates cand : Theta -> E -> ExchangeLaw and a selection select : Theta -> Prop, every two candidates whose executions generate the same courses (SameCourses: in every situation the same levels and the same take and give for every formation at every step) are either both selected or both not selected. The selection is constant on classes of candidates with identical courses.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (cand, select), with law, part, present, start as section variables: forall theta theta', SameCourses (cand theta) (cand theta') -> (select theta <-> select theta')
rows.beside: Same shape as Learning's Training.Through (alike := SameCourses on candidates) and as Web.SelectsThrough (Selection.lean) over courses instead of histories; no theorem ties Reads to either by name. Tied in the module: TrainsThrough.reads (a TrainsThrough selection, constant on candidates alike through r's couplings up to T, satisfies Reads); trained_alike_of_along uses Reads to conclude select theta <-> select theta'.
rows.docstring: "A training over the candidates `cand`, each executed in each situation, reads each candidate through its courses: candidates with the same courses are selected alike."

rows.name: Training.ReadsThrough
rows.states: For a lumping rho of histories, a part and an act law a: for every member h of the part (part h = true), every step t and every two level histories l, l' that rho lumps together for h at t, the law a gives h the same take and give for every condition across the step from t (ExchangeLaw.GivesAlike t h l l'). The members' exchange depends on the history only through rho's classes.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (rho : Lumping F C, part : F -> Bool, a : ExchangeLaw F C)
rows.beside: ExchangeLaw.Through (Counterfactual.lean) is the same relation for the coupling lumping, stated for non-members; ExchangeLaw.Nonanticipating is the same for the agreement lumping. Theorems: ReadsThrough.of_through (a.Through W obs (fun h => !part h) -> ReadsThrough (Lumping.coupling W obs) part a), ReadsThrough.through (the converse), ReadsThrough.of_nonanticipating (a.Nonanticipating -> ReadsThrough Lumping.agreement part a). Learning.Lumped is the analogue for a plain function lumped by pi.
rows.docstring: "An act law reads through a lumping for the part: each member exchanges alike under histories it lumps together up to the step."

rows.name: Transactions.Readings
rows.states: An assignment to each domain (a Nat) of either nothing or one Observation (epoch, serial, address, optional key): the reports the domains give about an installation.
rows.shape: abbrev for a FUNCTION type Domain -> Option Observation
rows.beside: Its twin for issuers is Approvals := Domain -> Option Request. No dependence relation is involved; the tie to the installation is the premise `faithful` (reads d = some o -> o = observed w p.address) in accepted_reading_matches and gate_route.
rows.docstring: "The readings of the domains."

rows.name: Transactions.faithfulReads
rows.states: For an installation w and request p, the assignment in which every domain reports some (observed w p.address): the installation's own epoch, serial, the request's address and the key located at that address in w's tree.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Installation -> Request -> Readings (a constant report for every domain)
rows.beside: Paired with faithfulApprovals; used in the worked examples (single_issuer_rejected, the two-domain shutdown, consumed-request theorems). It satisfies the `faithful` premise of accepted_reading_matches for any bad set; no theorem states that by name.
rows.docstring: "Every reader reports the installation."

rows.name: Transactions.readSupport
rows.states: For a request p, an assignment of reports and a domain d, true exactly when d's report equals some (expected p), i.e. d reports the epoch, serial, address and key the request expects. It is the per-domain support fed to the fault-envelope certificate in gate.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Request -> Readings -> Domain -> Bool
rows.beside: Its twin is approvalSupport (true when d approves exactly p). Theorem accepted_reading_matches: if every roster domain outside an admitted bad set reports only observed w p.address and certificate roster faults (readSupport p reads) = true, then expected p = observed w p.address; gate_route builds on it.
rows.docstring: "A domain supports a request's reading where it reports what the request expects."

rows.name: field reads
rows.states: Not a structure field: no structure in the module (Scope, Installation, Request, Observation, Outcome) has a field named reads. `reads : Readings` is an explicit parameter (or section variable) of gate, passGate, execute and the theorems about them: the domains' reports passed to the gate.
rows.shape: PARAMETER of type Readings (Domain -> Option Observation), not a field
rows.beside: none found beyond Readings and readSupport above; also readFaults (the fault envelope for reporters) and readBad / readFaithful / readResponses as hypothesis names in the certificates-available theorems.
rows.docstring: none

rows.name: TreeSearch.read
rows.states: For a search configuration s, the Scan made of its verdict (found t if a ticket is held, exhausted if the frontier is empty, pending otherwise) and its count of inspections made. It is a projection of the configuration onto the scan's two fields; no dependence relation is stated.
rows.shape: FUNCTION Search -> Scan, read s = <verdict s, s.inspected>
rows.beside: No read-free alternative name. Theorems tying it to the scan: orbit_reads_scan (read (Law.orbit advance <f, none, 0> n) = scan n f), run_reads_scan and run_reads_discover (along every run from the start, read (r.state n) = scan n f / discover n root), found_without_reading_rest. Here 'read' means 'the scan a configuration corresponds to'.
rows.docstring: "What a configuration reads as a scan."

rows.name: Learning.Cue.read
rows.states: For an occasion i = (cue, content) : Bool x Bool, the proposition that the cue is up, i.1 = true. It marks the occasions that serve as the data D: the selection is through agreement on them (Training.AgreeOn read), and Determines / Free are taken with read as the data.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on Occasion (Bool x Bool), i.e. a SET of occasions
rows.beside: It is an instance of the data predicate D in Learning.Determines, Learning.Free and Training.AgreeOn (Learning.lean). Theorems: Cue.seen_twin (with the identity lumping, a selected twin agreeing on every occasion where read holds and acting otherwise at (false, true)), Cue.unseen_fixed (Determines (Lumped (fun i => i.2)) read (false, true), via lumped_determines).
rows.docstring: "Read exactly where the cue is up."

rows.name: Unread (as the module uses it)
rows.states: The module defines no declaration named Unread. An 'unread occasion' is an input x with not D x (not R x) for the data predicate; the module's content is two relations at such x from Learning: Determines (Lumped pi) D x (within functions constant on pi's classes, equal values on D force equal values at x), which holds exactly when some d with D d has pi d = pi x (determines_lumped_iff, for D a list and two distinct values); and Free (Lumped pi) D x (any member's values on D combine with any value at x) when no d in D shares x's pi-class (free_lumped). In determines_iff_not_not, `unread` is only a hypothesis name for not P.
rows.shape: no definition; the relations are PREDICATES Determines and Free on (class of functions, data predicate, input) from Learning.lean
rows.beside: Learning.Determines, Learning.Free, Learning.Lumped, Training.Through, Training.AgreeOn. Theorems: free_lumped (no data in x's class -> Free (Lumped pi) D x), twin_selected (from free_lumped and Training.unselected_beyond_data), lumped_determines and determines_lumped_iff (Learning.lean), determines_iff_not_not (one occasion, data where P: Determines iff not not P).
rows.docstring: module title: "What readings fix of what is not read (未读之定)"

rows.name: Learnable.ReadOff
rows.states: For every configuration s, the feature val at s equals G applied to the sequence k ↦ some (reg (orbit of next from s, k steps on)). The feature is a function of the future of s under the law taken through the map reg: val = G ∘ (future through reg). Direction: val is determined by (factors through) that future sequence.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (next : S → S, reg : S → R, val : S → V, G : (Nat → Option R) → V); a Prop: ∀ s, val s = G (fun k => some (reg (Law.orbit next s k)))
rows.beside: Law.SameFuture (Recurrence.lean: ∀ n, o (orbit next s n) = o (orbit next s' n)) names the equivalence that ReadOff factors through. No theorem states ReadOff ↔ (SameFuture → val equal). The ties are: Learnable.learnable_iff (Learnable.lean), where learnability ↔ features agreeing from some step on across Law.SameFuture; Learnable.reads_of_agree, where agreement across SameFuture gives val = fromWorld … of the future; Learnable.learnable_iff_reading, where learnability ↔ ∃ G (respecting pointwise equality) with val equal to G of the future from some step on, which is the eventual form of ReadOff. ReadOff itself is used only in reading_predicts.
rows.docstring: A feature is read off the future through the map by `G`: at every configuration, it is `G` of the values through the map along the orbit from there.

rows.name: Learnable.readAt
rows.states: Given a list l of configurations and a sequence f : Nat → Option R, it returns the first x in l such that the first 2|l| − 1 entries of f equal the first 2|l| − 1 values through reg along the orbit starting from orbit next x |l|. It returns none if no x in l fits. It is a lookup: a configuration of the list whose future |l| steps on, through the map, matches f on a prefix of length 2|l| − 1.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from (next : S → S, reg : S → R, l : List S, f : Nat → Option R) to Option S, built with Identification.firstFit over l
rows.beside: Used in fromWorld (val of the found x, |l| steps on, with default v₀). The match on a 2|l| − 1 prefix is turned into Law.SameFuture by Law.sameFuture_iff_below inside Learnable.reads_of_agree. No name without 'read' for this lookup.
rows.docstring: The configuration of `l` read for a future: the first whose configuration as many steps on as the list is long has that future through the map before `2N - 1`.

rows.name: Learnable.reading
rows.states: Given G : (Nat → Option R) → V and a prefix r : List R, it returns some (G applied to the sequence k ↦ what the lasso-elimination extrapolation, unrolled on its own proposals, proposes k steps ahead of r). It is the extrapolation that runs the fixed lasso extrapolation forward without end and applies G to the result.
rows.shape: FUNCTION from G : (Nat → Option R) → V to an extrapolation List R → Option V: reading G r = some (G (Learning.ahead (Learning.byElimination Learning.lassos) r))
rows.beside: No name without 'read' for it. Ties: Learnable.reading_predicts (ReadOff + G respecting pointwise equality → PredictsFrom … (reading G) s from Identification's bound on); Learnable.reading_predicts_from (the eventual version); Learnable.learnable_iff_reading (an extrapolation exists ↔ some G works from some step on; the ← direction uses reading G); LearnableRuns.learnable_iff_reading (along runs). The lemma reads_of_agree is a theorem about fromWorld, not about reading.
rows.docstring: The extrapolation given a reading of futures: it unrolls the extrapolation by elimination over the lasso candidates and proposes the reading of what that proposes ahead.

rows.name: Weighting.ReadsSetsOn
rows.states: On the pair a, b: R ranks a above b exactly when O ranks kept a above kept b, and R ranks b above a exactly when O ranks kept b above kept a. On that one pair, the ranking R of presentations agrees, both ways, with the order O on courses composed with kept. The relation is R ↔ O ∘ kept, restricted to {a, b}.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (kept : P → X → Bool, R : P → P → Prop, O : (X → Bool) → (X → Bool) → Prop, a b : P): (R b a ↔ O (kept b) (kept a)) ∧ (R a b ↔ O (kept a) (kept b))
rows.beside: No name without 'read' in Weightings or its imports (Boundaries, GroupEnding). It is a pair-local 'R factors through kept'. Theorems using it: Weighting.reads_increasingAt, Weighting.narrower_above_net, Weighting.reads_ranksNet, Weighting.reads_increment_of, Weighting.reads_increment. No theorem derives it from ReadsSets, although it follows by instantiation. Also, in this docstring '`R b a` reads "`a` is ranked above `b`"' is a notation gloss, a different sense of 'read'.
rows.docstring: A ranking of presentations reads the sets on the pair `a`, `b`: it ranks them, each way, as the order `O` ranks the courses they keep.

rows.name: Weighting.ReadsSets
rows.states: For every pair a, b: R ranks a above b exactly when O ranks kept a above kept b. The ranking of presentations is the order on courses pulled back along kept, so two presentations that keep the same course are ranked alike. Wording and order of telling make no difference.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (kept : P → X → Bool, R : P → P → Prop, O : (X → Bool) → (X → Bool) → Prop): ∀ a b, R b a ↔ O (kept b) (kept a)
rows.beside: No name without 'read' (no DependsOnlyOn-style name in this module). It is 'R depends only on kept / factors through kept'. Theorem: Weighting.reads_ranksNet_widens (ReadsSets under ranksNet with every listed item weighing above zero → never a narrowing above its widening). No named theorem ReadsSets → ReadsSetsOn.
rows.docstring: A ranking of presentations reads the sets: on every pair it ranks as `O` ranks the courses kept, so it depends on the courses alone, not on how they are told.

rows.name: reads (parameter of Pace.turn / step / paced)
rows.states: reads : Nat → Bool is a schedule of step counts. At a step t where reads t = true, the rule's next value is h (x t) (g t), a function of the fast configuration and the rule. Where reads t = false, the rule's next value is g t, unchanged. 'A reading step' is a t with reads t = true. 'A rule that never reads' is ∀ t, reads t = false, so the rule is constant (rule_kept) and the same for any two starting fast configurations (rule_unreached).
rows.shape: FUNCTION Nat → Bool (the set of update steps); turn : Bool → S × R → S × R selects between (f x g, h x g) and (f x g, g)
rows.beside: No name without 'read'. Theorems: Pace.rule_kept, Pace.never_reads_course, Pace.rule_unreached, Pace.never_reads_lost/merged/loses, Pace.rule_until_reading, Pace.rule_alike_until_reading, Pace.rule_at_reading, Pace.paced_stretch ('the rule is not read' = reads false over a stretch), Pace.Copying.rule_parts.
rows.docstring: and the rule changes only at reading steps, `g (t + 1) = h (x t) (g t)` where `reads t` and `g (t + 1) = g t` elsewhere.

rows.name: 'neither level's step reads the fast configuration' (hypotheses of turn_byRule, byRule_reabsorbed)
rows.states: ∀ x x' g, f x g = f x' g and ∀ x x' g, h x g = h x' g. The next fast configuration and the next rule are the same for any two fast configurations with the same rule, so they depend on the rule alone. Here 'reads' means 'depends on', a different relation from the update schedule above.
rows.shape: PREDICATE (two hypotheses) on f : S → R → S and h : S → R → R: constancy in the first argument
rows.beside: Pace.byRule_reabsorbed is stated to be the instance of Law.perturbation_reabsorbed (Becoming.Capture), with the rule and step count as that law's rule. Its premise is a 'next depends only on the rule' condition. Pace names no DependsOnlyOn-style predicate for it.
rows.docstring: Where neither level's step reads the fast configuration, one turn does not either.

rows.name: 'read through a map' / 'read whole' (heldCourse, paced_held, stretch_fixed, whole_fixed)
rows.states: 'Read through o' means composed with a map o : S → O: heldCourse f g o x t = o (state t of the run of y ↦ f y g from x). 'Read whole' means the course of configurations itself, with no map: whole_fixed concerns (Law.run next s).state directly. pace_law's 2N − 1 bound is for courses composed with a map; whole_fixed's N + 1 is for uncomposed courses. 'What one level reads of another' in the docstring is this composition.
rows.shape: FUNCTION heldCourse : (S → R → S) → R → (S → O) → S → Nat → O; the 'whole' case is the identity map (no definition)
rows.beside: No name without 'read'. Theorems: Pace.paced_held, Pace.held_fixed (instance of Identification.bounded_agree), Pace.stretch_fixed, Pace.pace_law, Pace.whole_fixed, Pace.whole_fixed_exact.
rows.docstring: The course a rule generates where it is held from the fast configuration `x`, read through `o`: the run of the law the held rule gives.

rows.name: 'reads … only through what a pool reads' (rule_through_pool, its variable named read)
rows.states: Hypothesis ∀ x g, h x g = H (read x) g, with read : S → O. The rule update factors through a map of the fast configuration, so h depends on x only via read x. The theorem: at an update step r, two courses with the same rule at r and equal read-values of their fast configurations at r have the same rule at r + 1.
rows.shape: PREDICATE (factorisation hypothesis) on h : S → R → R, a map read : S → O and H : O → R → R; theorem conclusion is an equality of rules
rows.beside: No name without 'read'. It is a factor-through (DependsOnlyOn-like) premise stated inline; no tie to Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn (not imported). Theorem: Pace.rule_through_pool, which uses rule_at_reading.
rows.docstring: Where the rule reads the fast configuration only through what a pool reads of it (`h x g = H (read x) g`), two courses with one rule at a reading step, whose fast configurations the pool reads alike there, have one rule after it

rows.name: Web.SelectsThrough
rows.states: For all level histories l, l': if l and l' are alike through f's couplings at every step up to t (AlikeThroughUpTo obs f l l' t), then select l ↔ select l'. The selection gives the same verdict on histories that agree on what couples into f up to t. It is invariant under, or factors through, that equivalence.
rows.shape: PREDICATE on (W : Web F C, obs : F → C → Prop, f : F, t : Nat, select : (Nat → C → Nat) → Prop)
rows.beside: It is defined from AlikeThroughUpTo (Testing.lean). Tie: Web.selects_alike_iff ((∀ select, SelectsThrough … select → (select l ↔ select l')) ↔ AlikeThroughUpTo obs g l l' t); Web.class_selects; Web.separates; Web.SelectsThrough.excludes_iff. Nat-valued analogue: Web.ScoresThrough; group version Web.SelectsThroughAll / AlikeThroughAll (SelectsThrough.all). Closure: SelectsThrough.later, .widen, .not, .and. The parameter is named obs ('observe'), though it means 'c couples into g'.
rows.docstring: A selection is through `f`'s couplings up to `t`: histories alike through `f`'s couplings up to `t` are selected alike.

rows.name: Web.AlikeThroughUpTo
rows.states: For every step s ≤ t, AlikeThrough obs g l l' s holds. AlikeThrough at s means W.Admits (l s) s g ↔ W.Admits (l' s) s g, so the two histories admit g alike at s. It also requires l s c = l' s c for every condition c with obs g c, so every condition coupled into g has the same level in both histories at s. It relates two histories l, l' : Nat → C → Nat relative to formation g and step t.
rows.shape: PREDICATE (binary relation on level histories, parameterised by W, obs : F → C → Prop, g : F, t : Nat): ∀ s, s ≤ t → W.AlikeThrough obs g l l' s
rows.beside: It is itself the non-'read' name for the equivalence that 'a selection reads' summarises. It is an equivalence: AlikeThrough.refl, AlikeThroughUpTo.symm, AlikeThroughUpTo.trans. It defines Web.Excludes and Web.ClassThrough (Testing.lean). Tied to selection by Web.selects_alike_iff, Web.separates and Web.scores_alike_iff.
rows.docstring: Alike through `g`'s couplings at every step up to `t`.

families.relation: What a step gives (an exchange law's take and give, a member's act, a rule's next value, a level's next value) is the same wherever a named part of the configuration or of the level history is the same, so nothing outside that part makes a difference to it.
families.proposed_words: depends only on; goes alike. In the package: Mechanism.DependsOnlyOn, Laws.GoAlike, PartDependsOnlyOn, ExchangeLaw.GivesAlike, Nonanticipating (with AgreeUpTo), ExchangeLaw.Through, InsensitiveAt, Learning.Lumped. Proved ties exist for Unread -> GoAlike (goAlike_of_unread), ReadsBefore -> Nonanticipating, ReadsThroughOwn -> Through, ReadsThrough <-> Through, ReadsFinitely -> Nonanticipating, ReadsAt/ReadsInto <- Through.
members: Pace · 'neither level's step reads the fast configuration' (129)
Pace · rule_through_pool premise h x g = H (read x) g (131)
families.note: One relation, four ways the 'named part' is cut, which could be told apart in the wording: by time (17, 97, 105, 106: levels up to t, or up to t minus a delay), by place (22, 39, 48, 109, 110: neighbours, touched relata, marked conditions, a stock above its threshold), by coupling (85, 115, 3: what couples into the formation or the region), and by one argument dropped (9, 10, 54, 65, 129, 131: 'does not depend on' what lies beyond the share, on the own coupling, on the fast configuration). 27 and 96 are pointwise extensionality stated only because funext is avoided; they restrict nothing. 9 holds on all inputs and 65 only at the history the world produces. Most ties to DependsOnlyOn itself are by shape, not by theorem (Mechanism is often not imported).

families.relation: A verdict taken of a whole course, candidate or configuration (a selection, an answer, a score, a feature, a ranking, the truth of a statement) is the same on any two that a stated alikeness or map does not tell apart.
families.proposed_words: alike through; selects through. In the package: Web.AlikeThrough / AlikeThroughUpTo / AlikeThroughAll (133 is itself the word), Web.SelectsThrough / SelectsThroughAll, Web.ScoresThrough, Learning.Training.Through, Learning.Lumped, Law.SameFuture, SameCourses, Readout.ThroughParts; for the two statement rows the root's 'makes no difference to'.
members: FallibleInquiry · read with premise through, and Witness.read (31)
families.note: Same shape as the first family (constant on classes); kept apart because the thing that goes alike is a verdict on a whole course, not what a step gives. Three things could make it more than one: (a) 61 and 108 are statements whose truth a free slot (the order, the significance) makes no difference to, with 'alike' meaning the same dynamics; (b) 126 and 127 are iff, so the ranking is the pull-back along kept, stronger than factoring; (c) 94 runs the other way round from its sibling ThroughParts: the part is alike wherever the assigned function's value is alike (the function tells apart whatever the part tells apart). 41 and 112 are instances of the variable in 31; no theorem proves 41 respects AlikeThroughUpTo.

families.relation: A named thing's level or state enters another's exchange or next state, either as a relation, schedule or strength that is supplied, or because changing the first alone changes the second.
families.proposed_words: couples into; makes a difference to. In the package: CouplesAt, Couples, Upstream, OnLoop, Web.CoupledInto, CoupledIntoAt, the parameter obs, ExchangeLaw.RespondsWithin (strength), ExchangeLaw.carrying, ExchangeLaw.Sensitive, ¬Learning.Lumped, Tied (and its failure).
families.note: Two families if cut strictly. Supplied coupling (18, 19, 32, 34, 40, 49, 50, 104, 111): a relation obs, a Boolean schedule of marked levels, or a strength; the word is 'couples into' and the package has it (CouplesAt, CoupledInto). Coupling shown by a difference (36, 37, 45-47): flipping q changes k; an experiment's weights differ between two hypotheses; the word is 'makes a difference to' (Sensitive, not Tied). ReadsFinitely.least_coupling (Sensitive is the least coupling a law goes through) is the proved bridge between the two. 18, 19 and 32 are strengths computed from the level history itself (the coupling switches on at a threshold). 46 and 47 are data that only serve 45.

families.relation: A web (who is active, who draws on what, who requires what) is built from a flow or from a law's course: active exactly where it exchanges, drawing exactly where it takes, requiring a condition exactly where its exchange must stop once that level falls below the need.
families.proposed_words: For the slots: Flow.Exchanging, positive take, ExchangeLaw.RespondsBelow / MayRespondBelow, Web.Dependent. For the construction as a whole there is no word without the one in question ('the web derived from the exchange', 'the web the course shows').
families.note: The requirement slot is itself a 'makes a difference' relation (a level changed alone stops the exchange), so this family contains the third one inside it; RespondsBelow is not tied to Sensitive by any theorem. 52 is the existence statement (some relation generates this world), the others are constructions.

families.relation: The slower level's next value (the rule) is given as a function of the faster level's configuration: of the share alone, of the loss beyond it, of a pooled or windowed mix, or of nothing.
families.proposed_words: No word of its own for the map. Around it: Pace.turn / paced (the slot h), Drawn.pool, ClosedCapture.join, Stands K (the window), Ideals.Monotone (same relation as ReadsShare for a one-argument map, not tied by theorem). Plain names offered by the rows themselves: 'the share's rule update lifted to the pair', 'the constant rule hi', 'the rule as a function of the loss', 'the population-weighted pool of u and v', 'the paired update'.
families.note: These are maps, not relations; the relation each one bears is stated elsewhere: 'does not depend on what lies beyond the share' is Unread and ReadsThroughPresent (first family), 'no carrier of the beyond comes back' is NotReadmitted (kept family). 101 ReadsShare is the one relation here and is a different one: order-preserving in the share whatever the prior rule (monotone), which would make it a family of one. 12 and 56 are constant maps, so the word is doubly off for them. 15 also names a hypothesis (order.le v u) in Drawn. 66 is a course, named for the step from which the loss enters the pool.

families.relation: A step, a condition or an occasion lies inside or outside the set that a schedule visits or that a selection is fitted on.
families.proposed_words: ReadingSchedule.Within (every stretch of a steps contains a visit), 'schedule', 'update step'; Learning.Determines, Learning.Free, Training.AgreeOn, the data predicate D.
members: Unread · Unread as the module uses it (122)
families.note: Two families if cut by kind: steps in time (75, 76, 128: when a condition is visited, when the rule is revised) and occasions in a data set (121, 122: where the selection was fitted, and what is fixed or free outside it). 75 is a homonym of ClosedCapture.Unread (first family). 128 is a different relation from 129 in the same module.

families.relation: A map sends each configuration (or mode, or route point) to a value and merges some of them, and a course, a family or another function is taken through that map; where two such maps of one thing exist, they may or may not agree.
families.proposed_words: Learning.Lumped (for what goes alike across the merged), Parting.course val r, Learning.prefixOf, the projection π of PartDependsOnlyOn, Readout.Decodes, SingleValued, Adequate and the inline 'forget' factoring, Revising.alike, Registration.Keeps, Contextual / Agree / Glues, Flow.Balances.
families.note: This is the map itself, the thing the first two families are stated relative to; the map carries no relation alone. 77 and 78 could be a family of their own: two accounts of one change (by standing, by exchange) that agree exactly where the flow balances. 7, 21, 93 and 130 are images or courses through the map; 1, 2, 6, 8, 98, 120, 100 are the maps. 100 is weakly placed (an end value fed to a sum).

families.relation: A code or form stands for a configuration, a sense or an answer, and the code-side relation gives back what the coded thing answers.
families.proposed_words: Presentation.encode, answers, Exact, Joint, probes, TellsApart, Formula.eval, records / observe; List.mapM in shape for 103.
families.note: 64 is evaluation of a formula with one slot filled (Formula.eval is the same thing by definition) and sits here only loosely. 107 is plain equality c n = x. No dependence is stated by any member.

families.relation: A value is taken at a position or step given by an index map: a token at a site, a quantity at a position in a list, a flow or a level at the step another clock's step corresponds to.
families.proposed_words: Copying.tick / steps and Supplies (the pending-list counterparts), Web.sample, Stutter and Stutter.Moves, Tower.refine, pick, the siblings beforeAt / afterAt / cellAt.

families.against_the_six:
Family numbers below follow the order of the families list (1 step depends only on; 2 verdict alike through; 3 couples into / makes a difference; 4 web built from an exchange; 5 the rule's revision as a map; 6 inside or outside what is visited or fitted on; 7 a map that merges; 8 code stands for; 9 taken at a position or step; 10 label a line carries; 11 apart while return is open; 12 kept / closed under; 13 role answering go or off; 14 reports; 15 replenishing units).

(1) A step's dependence on a level = family 1, the largest (20 rows). It is narrower than the table: it does not cover family 2 (a verdict on a whole course going alike, 14 rows), and 'which level' is family 3 (the coupling relation, schedule or strength itself).
(2) The kept relation between a state and the worlds it admits = family 12 (rows 79-82). The table adds two rows of the same closure shape from other modules: PoolFromCourse.NotReadmitted and LossMatching.Frame.ReadsAt.
(3) What a rule's revision counts (pool and window) = family 5 (13 rows, from ClosedCapture, DrawnShaping, PoolFromCourse, ReadInTime, RuleCapture). Its relations are filed elsewhere: ClosedCapture.Unread and ReadsThroughPresent in family 1, NotReadmitted in family 12, Pace's schedule of revision steps in family 6. ReadsShare (monotone in the share) sits in family 5 as a different relation.
(4) What raises a level toward a set level and is itself rebuilt = family 15 (2 rows).
(5) A variant a line carries that sets how the carrier acts = family 10 (8 rows); the table shows it holds two relations (the label picks the law; the label passes or is revised down the line).
(6) The gauge = family 11, but only row 69 is the gauge; rows 67-68 are the timing relation (first apart before no return) and 86 is a selection holding on a course that ends a line.

Which of the six the table does not show: none is absent; all six have rows. Three rest on rows that are not declarations carrying the word: (6) the gauge is two constructors, with 'gauge' in docstrings only; (4) the units are the field St.ages with Present; (2) the admitted-worlds predicate B is a parameter of the module.

Which families the six leave out: nine of the fifteen, 76 of the 133 rows: family 2 (verdict alike through: SelectsThrough, ReadOffCouplings, Training.Reads, ReadsSets, ReadsOnlyDynamics), family 3 (couples into / makes a difference: Relay.reads, readCouplings, HexagramSequences.Reads), family 4 (the web built from an exchange: Flow.readOff, readWeb, readWorld), family 6 (schedule and data coverage), family 7 (the merging map and courses through it), family 8 (code and what it stands for), family 9 (value taken at a position or step), family 13 (the role answering go or off) and family 14 (reports of an installation). Family 2 and family 3 are the ones a five-module cut most misleads about, since together with family 1 they are the dependence sense proper (48 rows) and the package has words for all three.

families.summary: Sorted by the relation stated, the 133 rows fall into fifteen families, six of which split again on a strict cut, so the one word stands for about fifteen to twenty relations; four rows are not placed (one false match, one cost charge, two constructions). The largest is 'what a step gives depends only on a named part' (20 rows), and with its two neighbours, 'a verdict goes alike through an alikeness' (14) and 'couples into / makes a difference to' (14), the dependence sense covers 48 rows. Those three have words in the package and the root (DependsOnlyOn, GoAlike, GivesAlike, Nonanticipating, Through; AlikeThroughUpTo, SelectsThrough, Lumped; CouplesAt, CoupledInto, Sensitive), as do kept/closed under («闭», ClosedUnder), the carried label (RevisesBy, withAct), apart-in-time (FirstApart, TellsApartAt, Recoverable), code (encode, answers, Exact, eval), taken-at-a-step (sample, Stutter, tick), coverage (Within, Determines, Free), the merging map (course, prefixOf, Contextual), the go-or-off role (byRule) and the replenishing units (Present, Source). No word without the one in question exists for the rule's revision map (13 rows), for the web built from an exchange (5 rows, though its slots have Exchanging and RespondsBelow), or for the reports (7 rows, whose twin on the issuing side is named Approvals). The six-way cut from five modules matches six of the fifteen families and leaves out nine holding 76 rows; only the go-or-off role (4 rows) names a party standing over against a candidate. This is a reading of the supplied descriptions, with five doubtful rows checked against their Lean docstrings; nothing was edited, built or run.
